title: Melbourne Weeds & Garden Escapes
description: Introduced herbs, weeds and garden escapes you will meet around Greater Melbourne.
attribution: Species lists and photos: iNaturalist contributors (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA). Text: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0).

cards.name: Ribwort Plantain
cards.subtitle: Plantago lanceolata
cards.description: Plantago lanceolata is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae. It is known by the common names ribwort plantain, narrowleaf plantain, English plantain, ribleaf, lamb's tongue, and buckhorn. It is a common weed on cultivated or disturbed land.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is a rosette-forming perennial herb, with leafless, silky, hairy flower stems, growing to 45 centimetres (17+1⁄2 in) tall, exceptionally 100 cm (39 in). The basal leaves are lanceolate spreading or erect, scarcely toothed with 3–5 strong parallel veins narrowed to a short petiole.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Petr Harant, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Petr Harant

cards.name: Capeweed
cards.subtitle: Arctotheca calendula
cards.description: Arctotheca calendula is a plant in the sunflower family commonly known as capeweed, plain treasureflower, cape dandelion, or cape marigold because it occurs in the Western Cape Province in South Africa. It has a wide distribution in coastal areas of South Africa, extending from Namaqualand to Cape Point and as far as KwaZulu-Natal.
cards.keyFeatures: Arctotheca calendula is a squat perennial or annual herb which grows in rosettes and sends out stolons and can spread across the ground quickly. The leaves are covered with white woolly hairs, especially on their undersides.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Three-cornered Garlic
cards.subtitle: Allium triquetrum
cards.description: Allium triquetrum is a bulbous flowering plant in the genus Allium native to the Mediterranean basin. It is known in English as three-cornered leek or three-cornered garlic, in Australia as angled onion, and in New Zealand as onion weed. Both the English name and the specific epithet triquetrum refer to the three-cornered shape of the flower stalks.
cards.keyFeatures: Allium triquetrum produces stems that are 17–60 cm (6+3⁄4–23+1⁄2 in) tall and concavely triangular in cross-section. During winter and spring, each stem produces an umbel inflorescence of 4–19 flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lucas Carbone, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lucas Carbone

cards.name: White Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium repens
cards.description: Trifolium repens, the white clover, is a herbaceous perennial plant in the bean family, Fabaceae (also known as Leguminosae). The species is native to Eurasia and is one of the most widely cultivated types of clover. It has been widely introduced worldwide as a forage crop, and is now also common in most grassy areas of North and South America, Australia and New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a low-growing herbaceous, perennial plant. The leaves are trifoliolate, smooth, elliptic to egg-shaped, long-petioled, and usually with light or dark markings.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tom Norton, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tom Norton

cards.name: Spear Thistle
cards.subtitle: Cirsium vulgare
cards.description: Cirsium vulgare, commonly known as spear thistle, bull thistle, or common thistle, is a species of the Asteraceae genus Cirsium, native throughout most of Europe (north to 66°N, locally 68°N), Western Asia (east to the Yenisei Valley), and northwestern Africa (Atlas Mountains). It is also naturalised in North America, Africa, and Australia and is an invasive weed in several regions.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a tall biennial or short-lived monocarpic thistle, forming a rosette of leaves and a taproot up to 70 cm (28 in) long in the first year, and a flowering stem 1–1.5 m (3 ft 4 in – 4 ft 11 in) tall in the second (rarely third or fourth) year. It can grow up to 1.8 metres (5 ft 11 in) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sandy Wolkenberg, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Sandy Wolkenberg

cards.name: English Daisy
cards.subtitle: Bellis perennis
cards.description: Bellis perennis ( BEL-iss pə-REN-iss), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy. To distinguish this species from other plants known as daisies, it is sometimes qualified or known as common daisy, lawn daisy or English daisy.
cards.keyFeatures: Bellis perennis is a perennial herbaceous plant growing to 20 centimetres (8 inches) in height. It has short creeping rhizomes and rosettes of small rounded or spoon-shaped leaves that are from 2 to 5 cm (3⁄4–2 in) long and grow flat to the ground.
cards.imageCredit: (c) m.dolores paderne sa…, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Soursob
cards.subtitle: Oxalis pes-caprae
cards.description: Oxalis pes-caprae is a species of tristylous yellow-flowering plant in the wood sorrel family Oxalidaceae. Oxalis cernua is a less common synonym for this species. It is commonly known as African wood-sorrel, Bermuda buttercup, Bermuda sorrel, buttercup oxalis, Cape sorrel, English weed, goat's-foot, sourgrass, soursob, or soursop; Afrikaans: suring; Arabic: hommayda (حميضة).
cards.keyFeatures: The Oxalis pes-caprae flower is actinomorphic, with a calyx composed of five free or slightly fused sepals, a sympetalous corolla composed of five fused petals, an androecium composed of ten free stamens in two ranks, and a compound pistil.
cards.imageCredit: (c) portioid, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by portioid

cards.name: Wandering Trad
cards.subtitle: Tradescantia fluminensis
cards.description: Tradescantia fluminensis is a species of spiderwort native to South America. It is one of several plants known by the common name wandering Jew. It is also known as small-leaf spiderwort, river spiderwort, inch plant, speedy Henry, wandering willie and wandering trad.
cards.keyFeatures: Tradescantia fluminensis is a perennial groundcover that spreads along the ground with soft, hairless stems and leaves. The fleshy stems root at any node that is on the surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Saryu Mae 前 朝琉, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Saryu Mae 前 朝琉

cards.name: Common Sow-thistle
cards.subtitle: Sonchus oleraceus
cards.description: Sonchus oleraceus is a species of flowering plant in the tribe Cichorieae of the family Asteraceae, native to Europe and Western Asia. It has many common names including common sowthistle, sow thistle, smooth sow thistle, annual sow thistle, puha (in New Zealand English, from Māori pūhā), hare's colwort, hare's thistle, milky tassel, milk thistle, and soft thistle.
cards.keyFeatures: This annual plant has a hollow, upright stem up to 30 to 100 centimetres (12 to 39 in) high. It prefers full sun, and can tolerate most soil conditions.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Colin Meurk, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Colin Meurk

cards.name: Common Selfheal
cards.subtitle: Prunella vulgaris
cards.description: Prunella vulgaris, the common self-heal, heal-all, woundwort, heart-of-the-earth, carpenter's herb, brownwort or blue curls, is an herbaceous flowering plant in the mint family (Lamiaceae).
cards.keyFeatures: Prunella vulgaris grows 5–30 cm (2.0–11.8 in) high, with creeping, square-ish, reddish stems branching at the leaf axils. The opposite leaves are lance-shaped or ovate, entire, and sometimes reddish at the tip.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Brady Reed

cards.name: Onion Grass
cards.subtitle: Romulea rosea
cards.description: Romulea rosea is a herbaceous perennial plant in the family Iridaceae. It is a small plant, usually less than 20 cm high, with grass-like leaves. The flowers, which appear in spring, are pink with a yellow throat.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Don Loarie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Don Loarie

cards.name: Scarlet Pimpernel
cards.subtitle: Lysimachia arvensis
cards.description: Lysimachia arvensis, syn. Anagallis arvensis, commonly known as scarlet pimpernel, red pimpernel, red chickweed, poor man's barometer, poor man's weather-glass, shepherd's weather glass or shepherd's clock, is a species of low-growing annual plant with brightly coloured flowers, most often scarlet but also bright blue and sometimes pink. The native range of the species is Europe and Western Asia and North Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: When found as a summer annual, the scarlet pimpernel has a low-growing creeping habit, but as a winter annual, it forms a half-rosette with an upright stem. It has weak sprawling stems with square cross-section growing to about 5–30 centimetres (2–12 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Blue Periwinkle
cards.subtitle: Vinca major
cards.description: Vinca major, the greater periwinkle, also sometimes called bigleaf periwinkle, large periwinkle or blue periwinkle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Apocynaceae, native to the Mediterranean region. Growing to 25 cm (10 in) tall and spreading indefinitely, it is an evergreen perennial, frequently used in cultivation as a ground cover.
cards.keyFeatures: Vinca major is a trailing vine, spreading along the ground and rooting along the stems to form dense masses of ground cover individually 2–5 metres (6+1⁄2–16+1⁄2 ft) across and up to 25 centimetres (10 in) high, perhaps even 50–70 cm (20–28 in).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Mentxuwiki, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: South African Weed Orchid
cards.subtitle: Disa bracteata
cards.description: Disa bracteata, also known as the bract disa, leek orchid or the South African weed orchid is a species of orchid native to South Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: This tuberous geophyte that typically grows up to 30 cm (12 in) tall, although there are records of taller specimens. The linear-lanceolate leaves are 4–12 cm (1.6–4.7 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Thiele, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Pale Pink-sorrel
cards.subtitle: Oxalis incarnata
cards.description: Oxalis incarnata is a species of flowering plant in the woodsorrel family known by the common names pale pink-sorrel and crimson woodsorrel. It is native to southern Africa, but it can be found on other continents where it is an introduced species, often the descendant of garden escapees. It is grown and kept as an ornamental plant.
cards.imageCredit: (c) kevin koen, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by kevin koen

cards.name: Creeping Buttercup
cards.subtitle: Ranunculus repens
cards.description: Ranunculus repens, the creeping buttercup, is a flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae, native to Europe, Asia and northwestern Africa. It is also called creeping crowfoot and (along with restharrow) sitfast.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a herbaceous, stoloniferous perennial plant growing up to 50 cm (20 in) tall. It produces prostrate, creeping stolons that root at the nodes and give rise to new plantlets, as well as more or less erect flowering stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Frank Vincentz, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Common Vetch
cards.subtitle: Vicia sativa
cards.description: Vicia sativa, known as the common vetch, garden vetch, tare or simply vetch, is a nitrogen-fixing leguminous plant in the family Fabaceae. It is now naturalised throughout the world, being absent only in Antarctica and the Arctic regions. The centre of diversity is thought to be the Fertile Crescent, although gold standard molecular confirmation is currently not available.
cards.keyFeatures: Vicia sativa is a sprawling annual herb, with hollow, four-sided, hairless to sparsely hairy stems which can reach two meters in maximum length. The leaves are stipulate, alternate and compound, each made up of 3–8 opposite pairs of linear, lance-shaped, oblong, or wedge-shaped, needle-tipped leaflets up to 35 millimeters (1+1⁄2 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gabriel Campbell-Martinez, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Gabriel Campbell-Martinez

cards.name: Paterson's Curse
cards.subtitle: Echium plantagineum
cards.description: Echium plantagineum, commonly known as purple viper's-bugloss, Paterson's curse or Salvation Jane, is a species of the genus Echium native to western and southern Europe (from southern England south to Iberia and east to the Crimea), northern Africa, and southwestern Asia (east to Georgia). It has also been introduced to Australia, South Africa, and United States, where it is an invasive weed.
cards.keyFeatures: Echium plantagineum is a winter annual plant growing to 20–60 cm tall, with rough, hairy, lanceolate leaves up to 14 cm long. The flowers are purple, 15–20 mm long, with all the stamens protruding, and borne on a branched spike.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter Warren

cards.name: Bristly Oxtongue
cards.subtitle: Helminthotheca echioides
cards.description: Helminthotheca echioides, known as bristly (or prickly) oxtongue, is a sprawling annual or biennial herb native to Europe and North Africa. It was originally placed within the genus Picris but is often separated within the small genus Helminthotheca alongside a few other (mainly North African) plants which also have the distinctive outer row of bracts around the flowerheads.
cards.keyFeatures: Bristly oxtongue is an annual to biennial herb with an erect or sprawling habit that grows up to 90 cm (35 in) tall (often up to 150 cm in fertile soils and shady places), with a solid, furrowed stem and spreading branches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jerry Lanfear, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jerry Lanfear

cards.name: Petty Spurge
cards.subtitle: Euphorbia peplus
cards.description: Euphorbia peplus (petty spurge, radium weed, cancer weed, or milkweed), is a species of Euphorbia, native to most of Europe, northern Africa and western Asia, where it typically grows in cultivated arable land, gardens and other disturbed land.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an annual plant growing to 5–30 cm (2–12 in) tall (most plants growing as weeds of cultivation tend towards the smaller end), with smooth hairless stems. The leaves are stalked, oval-acute, 1–3 cm (0.4–1.2 in) long, with untoothed margin.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas

cards.name: Red-flowered Mallow
cards.subtitle: Modiola caroliniana
cards.description: Modiola is a monotypic genus of plants in the mallow family containing the single species Modiola caroliniana, which is known by several common names including bristly-fruited mallow, Carolina bristlemallow, babosilla, and redflower mallow. It is a creeping perennial which is probably native to South America but which is widely naturalized throughout the tropical and warmer temperate world.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Arum Lily
cards.subtitle: Zantedeschia aethiopica
cards.description: Zantedeschia aethiopica, commonly known as calla lily, arum lily, and death lily, is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to southern Africa in Lesotho, South Africa, and Eswatini.
cards.keyFeatures: Zantedeschia aethiopica is a rhizomatous herbaceous perennial plant, evergreen where rainfall and temperatures are adequate, deciduous where there is a dry season. Its preferred habitat is in or on the banks of streams and ponds.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dominicus Johannes Bergsma, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Cat's-ears
cards.subtitle: Hypochaeris radicata
cards.description: Hypochaeris radicata, phonetically hy-poh-KAIR-iss rad-ee-KAY-tuh, is sometimes spelled Hypochoeris radicata and known as catsear, flatweed, cat's-ear, hairy cat's ear, or false dandelion. It is a perennial, low-lying edible herb often found in lawns. H. radicata has been used for both food and medinicinal purposes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Purple Woodsorrel
cards.subtitle: Oxalis purpurea
cards.description: Oxalis purpurea is a species of flowering plant in the woodsorrel family known by the common name purple woodsorrel. It is native to southern Africa, including South Africa, but it is known on most continents as an introduced species. It is cultivated as an ornamental plant.
cards.keyFeatures: This perennial herb grows from bulbs and produces a few basal leaves and flowers. The leaf is made up of three hairy leaflets of various shapes which are dark green in color, turning streaked and spotted with brown as they dry.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cecile Roux, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Cecile Roux

cards.name: Artichoke Thistle
cards.subtitle: Cynara cardunculus
cards.description: The cardoon (Cynara cardunculus ), also called the artichoke thistle, is a thistle in the family Asteraceae. It is a naturally occurring species that also has many cultivated forms, including the globe artichoke. It is native to the Mediterranean region, where it was domesticated in ancient times and still occurs as a wild plant.
cards.keyFeatures: The wild cardoon is a stout herbaceous perennial plant growing 0.8 to 1.5 m (31 to 59 in) tall, with deeply lobed and heavily spined green to grey-green tomentose (hairy or downy) leaves up to 50 cm (20 in) long, with yellow spines up to 3.5 cm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: White-flower Fumitory
cards.subtitle: Fumaria capreolata
cards.description: Fumaria capreolata, the white ramping fumitory or climbing fumitory, is an herbaceous annual plant in the poppy family Papaveraceae. It is native to Europe, western Asia and northern Africa and naturalised in southern Australia, New Zealand, and southern South America. Common names include also ramping fumitory, white fumitory, and white-flower fumitory.
cards.keyFeatures: Plants have stems to 1 metre (3 ft 3 in) long and sometimes climb. The leaves are pinnatisect.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sid Miller, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Coastal Galenia
cards.subtitle: Aizoon pubescens
cards.description: Aizoon pubescens (Galenia or Coastal Galenia) is a low-growing perennial herb in the family Aizoaceae. It is native to South Africa (Cape Provinces, Free State, and Northern Provinces) and naturalised elsewhere.
cards.keyFeatures: The species is prostrate or decumbent, with ovate to spatulate leaves which are covered with hairs when young. The flowers are white with a slight pink tinge, and yellow with age.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Moth Plant
cards.subtitle: Araujia sericifera
cards.description: Araujia sericifera is a perennial vining plant in the genus Araujia, of the family Apocynaceae, that is native to South America. The species was described in 1817 by the Portuguese botanist Félix de Avelar Brotero. The synonym Araujia hortorum is in more frequent use in New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: Araujia sericifera is a creeping vine that can climb up to 5–10 metres (16–33 ft) high. When broken it releases a milky, smelly exudate.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Miriam Sokhet, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Miriam Sokhet

cards.name: Common Dandelion
cards.subtitle: Taraxacum officinale
cards.description: Taraxacum officinale, the dandelion or common dandelion, is a herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the daisy family, Asteraceae. The common dandelion is well-known for its yellow flower heads that turn into round balls of many silver-tufted fruit, which disperse in the wind. These balls are sometimes called "clocks" or "blowballs".
cards.keyFeatures: Taraxacum officinale grows from a (generally unbranched) taproot and produces several hollow, leafless flower stems, typically 5–40 centimetres (2–15+3⁄4 inches) tall, but occasionally reaching up to 70 cm (28 in) tall. The stems can be tinted purplish, are upright or lax, and produce flower heads that are held as tall or taller than the foliage.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jason Grant, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jason Grant

cards.name: Purple Salsify
cards.subtitle: Tragopogon porrifolius
cards.description: Tragopogon porrifolius is a species of plant commonly known as purple or common salsify, oyster plant, vegetable oyster, Jerusalem star, Jack go to bed, goatsbeard, or simply salsify. These last two names are also applied to other species. It grows wild in many places and is one of the most widely known species of the salsify genus, Tragopogon.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant grows to 1.2 m (4 ft) in height. As with other Tragopogon species, its stem is largely unbranched and the leaves are somewhat grasslike, up to 30 cm (12 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Sweet Violet
cards.subtitle: Viola odorata
cards.description: Viola odorata is a species of flowering plant in the family Violaceae. The small hardy herbaceous perennial is commonly known as wood violet, sweet violet, English violet, common violet, florist's violet, or garden violet. The plant is native to Eurasia.
cards.keyFeatures: Viola odorata spreads with stolons (above-ground shoots). The plant reaches 15 centimetres (6 in) in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Björn Sothmann, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Björn Sothmann

cards.name: Common Centaury
cards.subtitle: Centaurium erythraea
cards.description: Centaurium erythraea is a species of flowering plant in the gentian family known by the names common centaury and European centaury. It is also commonly known as feverfoullie, gentian or centaury.
cards.keyFeatures: This is an upright biennial herb which reaches half a meter in height. It grows from a small basal rosette and bolts a leafy, upright stem which may branch.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Podschwit, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Harry Podschwit

cards.name: Greater Plantain
cards.subtitle: Plantago major
cards.description: Plantago major, the greater plantain, is a species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae. It is native to Eurasia and temperate Africa, and widely naturalised elsewhere. Greater plantain is not closely related to the fruit also known as plantain, which is a type of banana.
cards.keyFeatures: Plantago major is a herbaceous, perennial plant with a rosette of leaves 15–30 centimetres (6–12 inches), exceptionally 70 centimetres (28 inches), in diameter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) lemonsnapp, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Buck's-horn Plantain
cards.subtitle: Plantago coronopus
cards.description: Plantago coronopus, the buck's-horn plantain, is a herbaceous annual to perennial flowering plant in the family Plantaginaceae. Other common names in the US and Italy include minutina and erba stella.
cards.keyFeatures: Plantago coronopus produces a basal rosette of narrowly lance-shaped leaves up to 25 centimeters (9.8 in) long that are toothed or deeply divided. The inflorescences grow erect to about 4 to 7 cm (1.6 to 2.8 in) in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cesar Ormazabal, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cesar Ormazabal

cards.name: Mock Strawberry
cards.subtitle: Potentilla indica
cards.description: Potentilla indica, known commonly as false strawberry, mock strawberry, or Indian strawberry, (also snakeberry in North America) is a flowering plant in the family Rosaceae, native to West Asia to India, East Asia, and Southeast Asia. It has ternate foliage and an aggregate accessory fruit, similar to true strawberries of the genus Fragaria.
cards.keyFeatures: The herbaceous plant spreads along creeping stolons, rooting and producing plantlets at each node. The leaves are trifoliate, dark green, and somewhat thick.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alpsdake, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Madeira Winter Cherry
cards.subtitle: Solanum pseudocapsicum
cards.description: Solanum pseudocapsicum is a nightshade species with mildly poisonous fruit. It is commonly known as the Jerusalem cherry, Madeira winter cherry, xiuhecapatl (in Nahuatl, "windherb"), or ambiguously, "winter cherry". These perennials can be grown decoratively as house plants, but in some areas of South Africa, India, Australia and New Zealand it is regarded as a weed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eric Knight, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Inkweed
cards.subtitle: Phytolacca octandra
cards.description: Phytolacca octandra, also known as inkweed or red inkplant, is a herbaceous perennial plant in the pokeweed family Phytolaccaceae, originating from the Neotropical realm of the Americas.
cards.keyFeatures: Inkweed is a member of the family Phytolaccaceae, growing up to 1 metre (3+1⁄2 feet). The leaves measure 6–15 cm (2.4–5.9 in) in length.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dinesh Valke, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Bird's-eye Speedwell
cards.subtitle: Veronica persica
cards.description: Veronica persica is a flowering plant in the family Plantaginaceae. Common names include birdeye speedwell, common field-speedwell, Persian speedwell, large field speedwell, bird's-eye, or winter speedwell. The most widespread species of Veronica, it is native to western Asia but has been introduced worldwide.
cards.keyFeatures: Veronica persica is an annual that reproduces from seed. Its cotyledons are triangular with truncated bases.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Timur Kalininsky, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Timur Kalininsky

cards.name: Prickly Sowthistle
cards.subtitle: Sonchus asper
cards.description: Sonchus asper, the prickly sow-thistle, rough milk thistle, spiny sowthistle, sharp-fringed sow thistle, or spiny-leaved sow thistle, is a widespread flowering plant in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Sonchus asper is an annual or biennial herb sometimes reaching a height of 200 centimetres (6.6 ft) with spiny leaves and yellow flowers resembling those of the dandelion. The leaves are bluish-green, simple, lanceolate, with wavy and sometimes lobed margins, covered in spines on both the margins and beneath.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Michelle W. （鍾偉瑋）, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Michelle W. （鍾偉瑋）

cards.name: Wild Radish
cards.subtitle: Raphanus raphanistrum
cards.description: Raphanus raphanistrum, also known as wild radish, white charlock or jointed charlock, is a flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae. The species is native to western Asia, Europe and parts of Northern Africa. It has been introduced into most parts of the world and is regarded as a habitat threatening invasive species in many areas, for example, Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Wild radish is an annual that grows up to 75 centimetres (30 in) tall, variously branched to multi-stemmed, with a distinct slender taproot which does not swell like that of the cultivated radish. The stems are green and sometimes purple at the base and nodes, round in cross section and slightly ridged, and bristly-hairy all over.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Seaside Daisy
cards.subtitle: Erigeron karvinskianus
cards.description: Erigeron karvinskianus, the Mexican fleabane, is a species of daisy-like flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, native to Mexico and parts of Central America. Other common names include Latin American fleabane, Santa Barbara daisy, Spanish daisy, Karwinsky's fleabane, or bony-tip fleabane.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a vigorous, spreading perennial plant growing from woody rhizomes to a maximum height of 15 cm (5.9 in). Its leaves are located along the stem, the basal leaves dying off as the plant bolts.
cards.imageCredit: (c) rainerburkard, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by rainerburkard

cards.name: Pellitory-of-the-wall
cards.subtitle: Parietaria judaica
cards.description: Parietaria judaica, spreading pellitory, is a species of herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Urticaceae. It is native to the eastern Mediterranean and Middle East, and is widely established worldwide as an urban weed.
cards.keyFeatures: Spreading pellitory is a perennial herb about 50 cm (up to 110 cm) tall with an upright to sprawling untidy habit. Plants can have many branched stems, which are pink or red and slightly woody and brittle at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elizabete Marchante, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Elizabete Marchante

cards.name: Prickly Lettuce
cards.subtitle: Lactuca serriola
cards.description: Lactuca serriola, also called prickly lettuce, milk thistle (not to be confused with Silybum marianum, also called milk thistle), compass plant, and scarole, is an annual or biennial plant in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae. It has a slightly fetid odor and is commonly considered a weed of orchards, roadsides and field crops. It is the closest wild relative of cultivated lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.).
cards.keyFeatures: Lactuca serriola has a spineless reddish stem, containing a milky latex, growing up to 2 metres (6 ft 7 in). The leaves get progressively smaller as they reach its top.
cards.imageCredit: (c) George F Mayfield, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Ivy-leaved Toadflax
cards.subtitle: Cymbalaria muralis
cards.description: Cymbalaria muralis, commonly called ivy-leaved toadflax, is a low, spreading, trailing plant with small purple flowers, native to rocky habitats in southern Europe. It belongs to the plantain family (Plantaginaceae), and is introduced and naturalised in many other temperate locations. The flower stalk is unusual for seeking light until it is fertilized, after which it grows away from the light.
cards.keyFeatures: Cymbalaria muralis spreads quickly, growing 10–80 cm (3.9–31.5 in) tall. It is a biennial or short lived perennial plant.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Didier Descouens, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Garden Nasturtium
cards.subtitle: Tropaeolum majus
cards.description: Tropaeolum majus, the garden nasturtium, nasturtium, Indian cress or monk's cress, is a species of flowering plant in the family Tropaeolaceae. An annual or a short-lived perennial with disc-shaped leaves and brilliant yellow, orange or red flowers, it is of cultivated, probably hybrid origin. It is not closely related to the genus Nasturtium (which includes watercress).
cards.keyFeatures: It is a fast-growing plant, either annual or perennial, with trailing stems growing to 0.9–1.8 m (3–6 ft).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lek Khauv, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Hemlock
cards.subtitle: Conium maculatum
cards.description: Conium maculatum, commonly known as hemlock (British English) or poison hemlock (in North America), is a highly poisonous flowering plant and a nitrophile weed species in the carrot family Apiaceae. The plant is herbaceous, with no woody parts, and has a biennial lifecycle.
cards.keyFeatures: Conium maculatum is a herbaceous flowering plant that typically grows as a biennial, but can grow as a perennial on occasion. It is a nitrophile.
cards.imageCredit: (c) L.J. Lamera, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by L.J. Lamera

cards.name: Climbing Asparagus
cards.subtitle: Asparagus scandens
cards.description: Asparagus scandens (also known as climbing asparagus fern or krulkransie) is a flowering plant native to South Africa in the genus Asparagus. Despite one of its common names, it is not related to ferns.
cards.keyFeatures: A hardy scrambling or climbing perennial with finely divided leaf-like Cladodes and underground tuibers. It prefers shady areas and moisture, but can tolerate some drought.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: English Broom
cards.subtitle: Cytisus scoparius
cards.description: Cytisus scoparius (syn. Sarothamnus scoparius), the common broom or Scotch broom, is a deciduous leguminous shrub native to western and central Europe. In Great Britain and Ireland, the standard name is broom; this name is also used for other members of the Genisteae tribe, such as French broom or Spanish broom; and the term common broom is sometimes used for clarification.
cards.keyFeatures: Plants of C. scoparius typically grow to 1–3 metres (3+1⁄2–10 feet) tall, rarely to 4 m (13 ft), with main stems up to 5 centimetres (2 inches) thick, rarely 10 cm (4 in). Stems are ridged and green.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jonathan Eyestone, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jonathan Eyestone

cards.name: Dove's-foot Crane's-bill
cards.subtitle: Geranium molle
cards.description: Geranium molle, the dove's-foot crane's-bill or dovesfoot geranium, is an annual herbaceous plant of the family Geraniaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Geranium molle is a small plant reaching on average 5–30 centimetres (2.0–11.8 in) in height. It is a very branched plant, quite hairy, with several ascending stems.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Patrick Le Mao

cards.name: Wood Forget-me-not
cards.subtitle: Myosotis sylvatica
cards.description: Myosotis sylvatica, the wood forget-me-not or woodland forget-me-not, is a species of flowering plant in the family Boraginaceae, native to Europe. This spring-flowering plant and its cultivars, typically with blue flowers, are the familiar forget-me-nots of gardens.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a short-lived herbaceous perennial plant, growing to 12–30 cm (5–12 in) tall by 15 cm (6 in) wide, with hairy leaves and a profusion of flowers with petals longer than their tube, pink in bud then opening disc-shaped, intensely sky-blue with yellow centres in spring. Stace (2011) describes this plant as having the following characteristics:
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Common Chickweed
cards.subtitle: Stellaria media
cards.description: Stellaria media, chickweed, is an annual flowering plant in the family Caryophyllaceae. It is native to Eurasia and naturalized throughout the world, where it is a weed of waste ground, farmland and gardens. It is sometimes grown as a salad crop or for poultry consumption.
cards.keyFeatures: Chickweed is a hardy annual which flowers throughout the year in northern Europe, in mild weather. The stems are terete and glabrous with a lax and sprawling growth habit, up to 40 cm (16 inches) long and 1 millimetre (1⁄16 in) in diameter, with a line (very occasionally 2 lines) of hairs running straight down its length, alternating sides at the nodes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Pablo, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Pablo

cards.name: Herb Robert
cards.subtitle: Geranium robertianum
cards.description: Geranium robertianum, commonly known as herb-robert or, in North America, as Robert's geranium, is a species of cranesbill that is widespread throughout the northern hemisphere and introduced to some countries in the southern. It is common in woods, hedges, gardens, and on waste ground, and can also be found on shingle beaches and limestone pavements.
cards.keyFeatures: Herb-robert is a small, usually biennial but sometimes annual or even short-lived perennial herb that typically grows to about 30 cm (1 ft) tall and broad, or sometimes up to about twice that size.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gilles San Martin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Gilles San Martin

cards.name: Sticky Mouse-ear Chickweed
cards.subtitle: Cerastium glomeratum
cards.description: Cerastium glomeratum is a species of flowering plant in the family Caryophyllaceae known by the common names sticky mouse-ear chickweed and clammy chickweed. It is native to Europe, Macaronesia to Assam but is known on most continents as an introduced species. It grows in many types of habitat.
cards.keyFeatures: This is an annual herb growing from a slender taproot. It produces a branched stem up to 45 centimeters (18 in) tall, with abundant glandular and non-glandular hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gilles San Martin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Gilles San Martin

cards.name: Spotted Medick
cards.subtitle: Medicago arabica
cards.description: Medicago arabica, the spotted medick, spotted burclover, heart clover, is a flowering plant in the pea and bean family Fabaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a sprawling plant with a height of 20–60 centimetres (8–24 in). It usually has spotted trifoliate leaves, but the number of leaflets per leaf can sometimes be different.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Don Loarie, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Cut-leaved Crane's-bill
cards.subtitle: Geranium dissectum
cards.description: Geranium dissectum or cut-leaved crane's-bill is a plant species of the genus Geranium. It is native to Europe. It can be found on other continents as well, in some instances as an introduced species.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Anne Parsons

cards.name: Blue Pimpernel
cards.subtitle: Lysimachia loeflingii
cards.description: Recorded 315 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Fourleaf Manyseed
cards.subtitle: Polycarpon tetraphyllum
cards.description: Polycarpon tetraphyllum, commonly known as four-leaved allseed (also fourleaf allseed or fourleaf manyseed), is a plant of the family Caryophyllaceae. An annual herb growing to 15 cm in height, it is found on sandy soils, in coastal areas and on wasteland. Native to Europe, it is also naturalised in parts of North America, Australia and elsewhere.
cards.keyFeatures: Polycarpon tetraphyllum is a prostrate, herbaceous, annual plant. The stems produce many branches, and leaves are obovate and glabrous.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by John Cowles

cards.name: Water Buttons
cards.subtitle: Cotula coronopifolia
cards.description: Cotula coronopifolia is a species of flowering plant in the aster family (Asteraceae). Commonly known as brass buttons, golden buttons, and buttonweed, it is native to southern Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: The flower heads are bright yellow discoid heads that look like thick buttons. Individual plants spread stems along the ground and send up the knobby flowers at intervals.
cards.imageCredit: (c) SABENCIA Guillermo César Ruiz, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Narrow-leaved Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium angustifolium
cards.description: Trifolium angustifolium is a species of clover known by the common names narrowleaf crimson clover, narrow clover and narrow-leaved clover.
cards.keyFeatures: Trifolium angustifolium is an annual herb growing erect in form. The leaves are divided into narrow leaflets which are linear to lance-shaped and measure up to 4.5 centimeters (1+3⁄4 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Anne Parsons

cards.name: Italian Arum
cards.subtitle: Arum italicum
cards.description: Arum italicum is a species of flowering herbaceous perennial plant in the family Araceae, also known as Italian arum and Italian lords-and-ladies. It is native to the British Isles and much of the Mediterranean region, the Caucasus, Canary Islands, Madeira and northern Africa. It is also naturalized in Belgium, the Netherlands, Austria, Argentina, North Island New Zealand and scattered locations in North America.
cards.keyFeatures: Arum italicum grows 30–46 cm (1–1.5 ft) high, with equal spread. It blooms in spring with white flowers that turn to showy red fruit.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Hop Trefoil
cards.subtitle: Trifolium campestre
cards.description: Trifolium campestre, commonly known as hop trefoil, field clover and low hop clover, is a species of flowering plant native to Europe and western Asia.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a herbaceous annual plant, growing to 10–30 centimetres (4–12 in) tall. The leaves are alternate and trifoliate, with three oblong or elliptical leaflets 4–10 millimetres (1⁄4–1⁄2 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Thiele, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Fennel
cards.subtitle: Foeniculum vulgare
cards.description: Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family. It is a hardy, perennial herb with yellow flowers and feathery leaves. It is indigenous to the shores of the Mediterranean but has become widely naturalized in many parts of the world, especially on dry soils near the sea coast and on riverbanks.
cards.keyFeatures: Foeniculum vulgare is a perennial herb. The stem is hollow, erect, and glaucous green, and it can grow up to 2.1 meters (7 feet) tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Common Agapanthus
cards.subtitle: Agapanthus praecox
cards.description: Agapanthus praecox (common agapanthus, blue lily, African lily, or lily of the Nile) is a popular garden plant around the world, especially in Mediterranean climates. It is native to the Kwa-Zulu Natal and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa. Local names include agapant, bloulelie, isicakathi and ubani.
cards.keyFeatures: Agapanthus praecox is a variable species with open-faced flowers. It is a perennial plant that can live for up to 75 years.
cards.imageCredit: (c) C T Johansson, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Ragwort
cards.subtitle: Jacobaea vulgaris
cards.description: Jacobaea vulgaris, synonym Senecio jacobaea, is a very common wild flower in the family Asteraceae that is native to northern Eurasia, usually in dry, open places, and has also been widely distributed as a weed elsewhere. Common names include ragwort, common ragwort, stinking willie, tansy ragwort, benweed, cushag, St. James-wort, stinking nanny/ninny/willy, staggerwort, dog standard, cankerwort, stammerwort.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is generally considered to be biennial but it has the tendency to exhibit perennial properties under certain cultural conditions (such as when subjected to repeated grazing or mowing). The stems are erect, straight, have no or few hairs, and reach a height of 0.3–2.0 metres (1 ft 0 in – 6 ft 7 in).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Mortin, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jon Mortin

cards.name: Bur Clover
cards.subtitle: Medicago polymorpha
cards.description: Medicago polymorpha is a plant species of the genus Medicago. Common names include California burclover, toothed bur clover, toothed medick and burr medic.
cards.keyFeatures: This weedy forb is an annual broadleaf plant. It inhabits agricultural land, roadsides and other disturbed areas.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Thiele, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Wild Carrot
cards.subtitle: Daucus carota
cards.description: Daucus carota, whose common names include wild carrot, European wild carrot, bird's nest, bishop's lace, carrot flower, and Queen Anne's lace (North America), is a flowering plant in the family Apiaceae. It is native to temperate regions of Afro-Eurasia with a number of regional subspecies, and is naturalised widely elsewhere.
cards.keyFeatures: The wild carrot is a herbaceous, somewhat variable biennial plant that grows to 30–100 cm (1–3 ft), rarely 120 cm (4 ft) tall, and is roughly hairy, with a stiff, solid stem. The leaves are tripinnate, finely divided and lacy, and overall triangular in shape.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eleftherios Katsillis, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eleftherios Katsillis

cards.name: Freesia
cards.subtitle: Freesia leichtlinii
cards.description: Freesia leichtlinii is a species of herb in the family Iridaceae, native to the Cape Provinces of South Africa. It is most widely known in its subspecies F. leichtlinii subsp. alba, commonly called Antique White Freesia, which has naturalized in California, the Mediterranean Basin, and parts of the Southern Hemisphere.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Di Turner

cards.name: Peruvian Lily
cards.subtitle: Alstroemeria aurea
cards.description: Alstroemeria aurea is a species of flowering plant in the family Alstroemeriaceae, native to Chile and Argentina, but naturalised in Australia, New Zealand and the United Kingdom. It is also widely cultivated as an ornamental.
cards.keyFeatures: Growing to 1 m (3.3 ft) tall by 0.5 m (1.6 ft) broad, it is a herbaceous perennial with brittle, fleshy roots beneath erect stems with narrow leaves. Many orchid-like flowers in brilliant shades of yellow and orange. appear in early to midsummer.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bárbara Daniela Jara Ríos, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bárbara Daniela Jara Ríos

cards.name: Tall Ramping-fumitory
cards.subtitle: Fumaria bastardii
cards.description: Fumaria bastardii, commonly, tall ramping fumitory or bastard's fumitory, is a tall (to 2 m.), many-branched herbaceous flowering plant native to Western Europe including the British Isles and the northern Mediterranean. The species is a weed of arable and disturbed ground, and occurs as an introduced alien in many areas of the world with suitable climates, including Southwest Australia and North America.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Dwarf Nettle
cards.subtitle: Urtica urens
cards.description: Urtica urens, commonly known as annual nettle, dwarf nettle, small nettle, dog nettle, burning nettle, or bush nettle is a herbaceous annual flowering plant species in the nettle family Urticaceae. It is native to Eurasia, including the Himalayan regions of Kalimpong, Darjeeling and Sikkim in India and can be found in North America, New Zealand and South Africa as an introduced species.
cards.keyFeatures: Urtica urens is an annual plant, monoecious (with male and female flowers on the same plant) and generally much shorter. It can be distinguished from the perennial and dioecious U. dioica (stinging nettle) by its more rounded leaves with coarser, deeper toothing and with the terminal tooth of similar length to the adjacent teeth.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Peppercorn Tree
cards.subtitle: Schinus areira
cards.description: Recorded 259 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jeremy James, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jeremy James

cards.name: Purple Cestrum
cards.subtitle: Cestrum elegans
cards.description: Cestrum elegans, the purple cestrum, red cestrum, or bastard jasmine, is a species of flowering plants in the genus Cestrum.
cards.keyFeatures: Cestrum elegans is a slender evergreen that reaches seven feet in height. Overall, the structure is very compact with only a few branches.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by April

cards.name: Sheep's Sorrel
cards.subtitle: Rumex acetosella
cards.description: Rumex acetosella, commonly known as red sorrel, sheep's sorrel, field sorrel and sour weed, is a species of flowering plant in the buckwheat family Polygonaceae. Native to Eurasia including the British Isles, the plant and its subspecies are common perennial weeds. It has green arrowhead-shaped leaves and red-tinted deeply ridged stems, and it sprouts from an aggressive and spreading rhizome.
cards.keyFeatures: Rumex acetosella is a perennial herb which spreads via rhizomes. It has a slender and reddish, upright stem that is branched at the top, reaching a height of 50 centimetres (20 inches).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Agnieszka Kwiecień, Nova, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Spring Starflower
cards.subtitle: Ipheion uniflorum
cards.description: Ipheion uniflorum is a species of flowering plant, related to the onions, placed in the allium subfamily (Allioideae) of the Amaryllidaceae. It is known by the common name springstar, or spring starflower. Along with all species of the genus Ipheion, some sources place it in the genus Tristagma, but research published in 2010 suggested that this is incorrect.
cards.keyFeatures: This is a small herbaceous perennial growing from a bulb and producing flat, shiny, green, hairless, grasslike leaves up to 30 cm (12 in) long. The foliage has an onion-like scent when crushed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Felipe Horton, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Felipe Horton

cards.name: St. John's Wort
cards.subtitle: Hypericum perforatum
cards.description: Hypericum perforatum, commonly known as St. John's wort (sometimes perforate St. John's wort or common St.
cards.keyFeatures: Hypericum perforatum is an herbaceous perennial plant with hairless (glabrous) stems and leaves. The root of each plant is slender and woody with many small, fibrous small side roots and also extensive, creeping rhizomes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Gyselinck, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Gyselinck

cards.name: Common Ramping-fumitory
cards.subtitle: Fumaria muralis
cards.description: Fumaria muralis, known as common ramping-fumitory or wall fumitory, is a flowering herbaceous plant in the poppy family (Papaveraceae) native to western Europe and northwestern Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: Fumaria muralis is a delicate annual plant that flowers in spring. It is most easily distinguished by its flowers, which have pink petals with dark red or purple tips.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Lesser Hop Trefoil
cards.subtitle: Trifolium dubium
cards.description: Trifolium dubium, the lesser trefoil, suckling clover, little hop clover or lesser hop trefoil, is a flowering plant in the pea and clover family Fabaceae. This species is generally accepted as the primary plant to represent the traditional Irish shamrock. It is native to Europe, but can be found in many parts of the world as an introduced species.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Common Hedge Parsley
cards.subtitle: Torilis arvensis
cards.description: Torilis arvensis is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae known by the common names spreading hedge parsley, tall sock-destroyer and common hedge parsley. It is native to parts of Europe and it is known elsewhere, such as North America, as an introduced species and a common weed. It grows in many types of habitat, especially disturbed areas.
cards.imageCredit: (c) odobenine, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by odobenine

cards.name: Onion Weed
cards.subtitle: Asphodelus fistulosus
cards.description: Asphodelus fistulosus is a species of plant known as hollow-stemmed asphodel, onionweed, onion-leafed asphodel, and pink asphodel. It is native to the Mediterranean region as well as the Arabian Peninsula, Transcaucasus, and Madeira. It is an invasive exotic weed in the United States, with significant infestations in California, Arizona, New Mexico, and Texas.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Small Melilot
cards.subtitle: Melilotus indicus
cards.description: Melilotus indicus, sometimes incorrectly written Melilotus indica, is a yellow-flowered herb in the Fabaceae family. It is native to northern Africa, Europe and Asia, but naturalized throughout much of the rest of the world's temperate climate zones. It is a commonly occurring weed in disturbed habitats, with historical uses for forage and medicine.
cards.keyFeatures: M. indicus is an annual herb from 10 to 50 centimetres (3.9 to 19.7 inches) in height (rarely to one meter), with compound leaves of trifoliate leaflets. Leaf edges are sharply dentate.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terry Woodward, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terry Woodward

cards.name: Purple Morning Glory
cards.subtitle: Ipomoea indica
cards.description: Ipomoea indica is a species of flowering plant in the family Convolvulaceae, known by several common names, including blue morning glory, oceanblue morning glory, koali awa, and blue dawn flower. It bears heart-shaped or three-lobed leaves and purple or blue funnel-shaped flowers 6–8 cm (2–3 in) in diameter, from spring to autumn. The flowers produced by the plant are hermaphroditic.
cards.keyFeatures: Ipomoea indica is a vigorous, long-lived, tender, perennial plant, a vine which is native to tropical, subtropical and warm temperate habitats throughout the world. It blooms all year long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) i_c_riddell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by i_c_riddell

cards.name: Belladonna Lily
cards.subtitle: Amaryllis belladonna
cards.description: Amaryllis belladonna, the Jersey lily, belladonna-lily, naked-lady-lily, or March lily, is a plant species native to Cape Province in South Africa but widely cultivated as an ornamental.
cards.keyFeatures: Perennial bulbous geophyte with one to two erect solid stems which appear in late summer. The inflorescence bears 2–12 showy fragrant funnel-shaped flowers on a 'naked' (leafless) stem, which gives it the common name of naked-lady-lily.
cards.imageCredit: (c) gailhampshire, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Whitetip Nightshade
cards.subtitle: Solanum chenopodioides
cards.description: Solanum is a large and diverse genus of flowering plants, which include three food crops of high economic importance: the potato, the tomato and the eggplant (aubergine, brinjal). It is the largest genus in the nightshade family Solanaceae, comprising around 1,500 species.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Joss Carr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Joss Carr

cards.name: Ox-eye Daisy
cards.subtitle: Leucanthemum vulgare
cards.description: Leucanthemum vulgare, commonly known as the ox-eye daisy, oxeye daisy, dog daisy, marguerite (French: Marguerite commune, "common marguerite") and other common names, is a widespread flowering plant native to Europe and the temperate regions of Asia, and an introduced plant to North America, Australia and New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: Leucanthemum vulgare is a perennial herb that grows to a height of 80 cm (31 in) and has a creeping underground rhizome. The lower parts of the stem are hairy, sometimes densely hairy but more or less glabrous in the lower parts.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Musk Stork's-bill
cards.subtitle: Erodium moschatum
cards.description: Erodium moschatum is a species of flowering plant in the geranium family known by the common names musk stork's-bill and whitestem filaree. This is a weedy annual or biennial herb which is native to much of Eurasia and North Africa but can be found on most continents where it is an introduced species.
cards.keyFeatures: Musk stork's-bill is an annual monoecious herb which grows as a sprawling, procumbent to erect plant up to about 60 cm long or tall, with a musky smell when bruised. It is almost entirely covered with either simple or sticky glandular hairs except for the fruits and petals.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Wills, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Wills

cards.name: Subterranean Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium subterraneum
cards.description: Trifolium subterraneum, the subterranean clover (often shortened to sub clover), subterranean trefoil, is a species of clover native to Europe, Southwest Asia, Northwest Africa and Macaronesia. The plant's name comes from its underground seed development (geocarpy), a characteristic not possessed by other clovers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John A Haskins, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by John A Haskins

cards.name: Small-flowered Mallow
cards.subtitle: Malva parviflora
cards.description: Malva parviflora is an annual or perennial herb that is native to Northern Africa, Southern Europe, and Western and Central Asia and is widely naturalized elsewhere. Common names include cheeseweed, cheeseweed mallow, Egyptian mallow, least mallow, little mallow, mallow, marshmallow, small-flowered mallow, small-flowered marshmallow, and smallflower mallow. It is used in traditional medicine.
cards.keyFeatures: M. parviflora has a decumbent or erect habit, growing up to 50–80 cm in height. The broad leaves have 5–7 shallow lobes and are 8–10 cm in diameter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Roberto Daniel Avila, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Roberto Daniel Avila

cards.name: Mediterranean Cabbage
cards.subtitle: Brassica fruticulosa
cards.description: Brassica fruticulosa, the Mediterranean cabbage or twiggy turnip, is a member of the agriculturally significant genus Brassica. It was described by Domenico Maria Leone Cirillo in 1792.
cards.keyFeatures: Brassica fruticulosa has a similar odour to cabbage and broccoli, when crushed. The plant's stem is smooth and erect, varies from grey to green in colour, and can reach a height of 50 centimetres.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Yellow Archangel
cards.subtitle: Lamium galeobdolon
cards.description: Lamium galeobdolon, the yellow archangel, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family Lamiaceae. It is native to Europe and western Asia but it is widely introduced in North America and elsewhere. It is the only species in the genus Lamium with yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Lamium galeobdolon sensu lato is a perennial plant with square stems growing from 15 to 60 cm (6 to 24 in) tall. The paired opposite leaves are stalked with toothed margins.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Paul Cook, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Paul Cook

cards.name: Flaxleaf Fleabane
cards.subtitle: Erigeron bonariensis
cards.description: Erigeron bonariensis is a species in the family Asteraceae, found throughout the tropics and subtropics as a pioneer plant; its precise origin is unknown, but most likely it stems from Central America or South America. It has become naturalized in many other regions, including North America, Europe and Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Erigeron bonariensis grows up to 75 cm (29.5 in) in height and its leaves are covered with stiff hairs, including long hairs near the apex of the bracts. Its flower heads have white ray florets and yellow disc florets.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Bulbil Bugle-lily
cards.subtitle: Watsonia meriana
cards.description: Watsonia meriana is a species of flowering plant in the family Iridaceae known by the common name bulbil bugle-lily. It is one of several Watsonia species known as wild watsonia. It is native to the Cape Provinces of South Africa, but it is well known as an ornamental plant grown in gardens for its showy spikes of flowers, and is an invasive species in areas where it has escaped cultivation.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a perennial herb growing from a fibrous-coated corm and growing to a maximum height well over one meter when in flower, sometimes reaching two meters. Each corm produces three or four erect, lance-shaped leaves that measure up to 60 centimeters long by 6 wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Vynbos, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Chris Vynbos

cards.name: Bear's Breeches
cards.subtitle: Acanthus mollis
cards.description: Acanthus mollis, commonly known as bear's breeches, sea dock, bear's foot plant, sea holly, gator plant or oyster plant, is a species of plant in the family Acanthaceae and is native to the Mediterranean region. It is a leafy, clump-forming perennial herb, with a rosette of relatively large, lobed or toothed leaves, and purplish and white flowers on an erect spike.
cards.keyFeatures: Acanthus mollis is a leafy, clump-forming perennial herb with tuberous roots. It has a basal rosette of dark glossy green, lobed or divided, glabrous leaves 50 cm (20 in) long and 30 cm (12 in) wide on a petiole 20–30 cm (7.9–11.8 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nathan Aaron, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Shepherd's-purse
cards.subtitle: Capsella bursa-pastoris
cards.description: Capsella bursa-pastoris, commonly known as shepherd's purse or lady's purse, is a small flowering plant in the mustard family. It has been described as a protocarnivore because its seeds contain mucilage, which traps nematodes. The plant is native to Eurasia but is naturalized and considered a common weed in many parts of the world, especially in colder climates.
cards.keyFeatures: Capsella bursa-pastoris is a ruderal and an annual or biennial plant. It grows from a rosette of lobed leaves at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Joss Carr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Joss Carr

cards.name: Square Stemmed Saint John's Wort
cards.subtitle: Hypericum tetrapterum
cards.description: Hypericum tetrapterum (syn. H. quadrangulum) is a herbaceous perennial plant species in the flowering plant family Hypericaceae. Its common names include St.
cards.keyFeatures: Hypericum tetrapterum is a rhizomatous, glabrous perennial plant growing up to 1.2 m (3 ft 11 in) in height. The stems are square in cross section, with conspicuous wings at the corners.
cards.imageCredit: (c) gill_ryenats, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by gill_ryenats

cards.name: Hare's Foot Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium arvense
cards.description: Trifolium arvense, commonly known as the hare's-foot clover, rabbitfoot clover, stone clover or oldfield clover, is a flowering plant in the bean family, Fabaceae. It is native to Europe.
cards.keyFeatures: Trifolium arvense is a small erect herbaceous annual or biennial plant, growing to 10–40 centimetres (4–15+1⁄2 in) tall. Like all clovers, its leaves are trifoliate, divided into three slender, sessile leaflets 1–2 cm (1⁄2–3⁄4 in) long and 3–5 millimetres (1⁄8–1⁄4 in) broad, sometimes edged with small hairs and finely serrated.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gilles San Martin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Gilles San Martin

cards.name: Curled Dock
cards.subtitle: Rumex crispus
cards.description: Rumex crispus, the curly dock, curled dock or yellow dock, is a perennial flowering plant in the family Polygonaceae, native to Europe and Western Asia.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant produces an inflorescence or flower stalk that grows to 1.5 metres (5 feet) high. It has smooth leaves shooting off from a large basal rosette, with distinctive waved or curled edges; these can grow to 14–24 centimetres (5+1⁄2–9+1⁄2 inches).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Wall Speedwell
cards.subtitle: Veronica arvensis
cards.description: Veronica arvensis, common names: wall speedwell, corn speedwell, common speedwell, rock speedwell, field speedwell, is an annual flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae. The species is native to Europe and a common weed in gardens, pastures, waste places, and cultivated land.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a hairy, erect to almost recumbent, annual herb, 9 to 40 centimetres (3.5 to 15.7 in) high from a taproot. The leaves are oppositely arranged in pairs about the stem.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Purpletop
cards.subtitle: Verbena bonariensis
cards.description: Verbena bonariensis, commonly known as the purpletop vervain, clustertop vervain, Argentinian vervain, tall verbena or pretty verbena, is a member of the verbena family cultivated as a flowering annual or herbaceous perennial plant.
cards.keyFeatures: Verbena bonariensis is a tall and slender-stemmed perennial. It can grow to 6 ft (1.8 m) tall and can spread to 3 ft (0.91 m) wide.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Di Turner

cards.name: French Flax
cards.subtitle: Linum trigynum
cards.description: Linum trigynum, the French flax, is a species of annual herb in the family Linaceae. It is native to Southern Europe, Western Asia, North Africa, the Horn of Africa and some oceanic islands, such as Madeira, Canary Islands and Socotra. They have a self-supporting growth form.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Mesaglio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Mesaglio

cards.name: Chicory
cards.subtitle: Cichorium intybus
cards.description: Common chicory (Cichorium intybus) is a somewhat woody, perennial herbaceous plant of the family Asteraceae, usually with bright blue flowers, rarely white or pink. Native to Europe, North Africa, and western Asia, it has been introduced to the Americas, Australia, and South Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: When flowering, chicory has a tough, grooved, and more or less hairy stem. It can grow to 1.5 metres (5 feet) tall.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Алексей Ябс

cards.name: Fairy Stonecrop
cards.subtitle: Crassula multicava
cards.description: Crassula multicava is a perennial succulent plant from the family Crassulaceae. It is also known under various English common names including the fairy crassula, pitted crassula and London pride. In Zulu, it is known as umadinsane, one of several plants known by this name.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a moderate to fast growing, mat-forming plant that features buxom, oval to round and deep green, opposite leaves, with one cultivar ('Purple Dragon') having purple undersides. The plant blooms in winter in its native habitat with white to pinkish starry flowers with four petals and four sepals.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bruce Calvert, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bruce Calvert

cards.name: Green Alkanet
cards.subtitle: Pentaglottis sempervirens
cards.description: Pentaglottis is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the family Boraginaceae. It is represented by a single species, Pentaglottis sempervirens, commonly known as green alkanet or evergreen bugloss, and it is one of several related plants known as alkanet. It is a bristly, perennial plant native to southwestern Europe, in northwest Iberia and France.
cards.keyFeatures: Pentaglottis sempervirens is a perennial, that has a deep tap root. It grows up to approximately 60–90 cm (23.6–35.4 in) tall with a roughly hairy stem.
cards.imageCredit: (c) anemoneprojectors (getting through the backlog), some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Friar's-cowl
cards.subtitle: Arisarum vulgare
cards.description: Arisarum vulgare, common name the friar's cowl or larus, is an herbaceous, perennial, rhizomatous plant in the genus Arisarum belonging to the family Araceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Arisarum vulgare reaches on average 10–30 centimetres (3.9–11.8 in) of height. The leaves of this geophyte plant are basal only, wide, ovate to arrow-shaped, with a petiole 12–15 centimetres (4.7–5.9 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) J. Sayers, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Snowflake
cards.subtitle: Leucojum aestivum
cards.description: Leucojum is a small genus of bulbous plants native to Eurasia belonging to the amaryllis family, subfamily Amaryllidoideae. As currently circumscribed, the genus includes only two known species, most former species having been moved into the genus Acis. Both species are known as snowflakes.
cards.keyFeatures: Until 2004, the genus Leucojum was treated as including species now placed in Acis. Leucojum when narrowly circumscribed consists of only two species, Leucojum aestivum and Leucojum vernum.
cards.imageCredit: (c) su neko, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Wild Gladiolus
cards.subtitle: Gladiolus undulatus
cards.description: Gladiolus undulatus is a plant species in the family Iridaceae.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gary Williams, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Gary Williams

cards.name: Broad-leaved Dock
cards.subtitle: Rumex obtusifolius
cards.description: Rumex obtusifolius, commonly known as bitter dock, broad-leaved dock, bluntleaf dock, dock leaf, dockens or butter dock, is a perennial plant in the family Polygonaceae. It is native to Europe, but is found on all temperate continents.
cards.keyFeatures: Rumex obtusifolius is a perennial herbaceous flowering plant that grows to a height of 40 to 150 cm (16 to 59 in). It is easily recognizable by its very large oval leaves with cordate bases and rounded tips, some of the lower leaves having red stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andreas Rockstein, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Small-flowered Catchfly
cards.subtitle: Silene gallica
cards.description: Silene gallica is a species of flowering plant in the family Caryophyllaceae known by several common names, including common catchfly, small-flowered catchfly, and windmill pink. It is native to Eurasia and North Africa, but it can be found throughout much of the temperate world as a common roadside weed.
cards.keyFeatures: Silene gallica is an erect or semi-erect annual herb growing up to 50 cm (20 in) tall, its branching stem clad in long, curling hairs and shorter, glandular hairs. The opposite, entire, lance-shaped leaves have acute apexes, are up to 3.5 cm (1.4 in) long on the lower parts of the plant, and smaller on the upper parts.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sid Miller, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Stinkwort
cards.subtitle: Dittrichia graveolens
cards.description: Dittrichia graveolens, commonly known as stinkwort or stinking fleabane, is a plant species in the sunflower family, native to southern Europe, North Africa, and western Asia as far east as Pakistan. It has become naturalized in California, Asia, Africa, Australia, and other places and is regarded as a noxious weed in some regions.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Fabien Piednoir, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Fabien Piednoir

cards.name: Orache
cards.subtitle: Atriplex prostrata
cards.description: Atriplex prostrata, called the spear-leaved orache, hastate orache, thin-leaf orache, triangle orache, and fat hen, is a widespread species of flowering plant in the saltbush genus Atriplex, native to Europe, Macaronesia, northern Africa, Ethiopia, the Middle East, western Siberia, and Central Asia, and introduced to temperate North America, South America, Australia, New Zealand, Korea, Japan, and Primorsky Krai in far eastern Russia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andreas Rockstein, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Butterfly Iris
cards.subtitle: Dietes grandiflora
cards.description: Dietes grandiflora, commonly named fortnight lily, large wild iris, African iris or fairy iris, is a rhizomatous perennial plant of the Iris Family (Iridaceae) with long, rigid, sword-like green leaves. This species is common in horticulture in its native South Africa, where it is often used in public gardens, beautification of commercial premises and along roadsides.
cards.keyFeatures: The blooms are white with yellow and violet markings and can be up to four inches (ten cm) in diameter. Dark markings are found at the base of the outer tepals.
cards.imageCredit: (c) J. Sayers, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Indian Fig
cards.subtitle: Opuntia ficus-indica
cards.description: Opuntia ficus-indica, the Indian fig opuntia, fig opuntia, or prickly pear, is a species of cactus that has long been a domesticated crop plant grown in agricultural economies throughout arid and semiarid parts of the world. O. ficus-indica is the most widespread and most commercially important cactus. It is grown primarily as a fruit crop, and also for the vegetable nopales and other uses.
cards.keyFeatures: O. ficus-indica is polyploid, hermaphroditic, and autogamous. As Opuntia species grow in semiarid environments, the main limiting factor in their environment is water.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Francesco Cecere

cards.name: Rough-fruited Buttercup
cards.subtitle: Ranunculus muricatus
cards.description: Ranunculus muricatus is a species of buttercup known by the common names rough-fruited buttercup and spinyfruit buttercup. It is native to Europe, but it can be found in many other places in the world, including parts of Africa, Australia, and the western and eastern United States, as an introduced species and agricultural and roadside weed. It grows in wet habitats, such as irrigation ditches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Don Loarie, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Nipplewort
cards.subtitle: Lapsana communis
cards.description: Lapsana communis, the common nipplewort, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is native to Europe and southwestern Asia, and it is widely naturalized in other regions including North America.
cards.keyFeatures: Lapsana communis is an annual or perennial herbaceous plant growing to 1–1.2 m (3 ft 3 in – 3 ft 11 in) tall, with erect, hairy branching stems and milky sap.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Carl Guyer

cards.name: Common Dog-violet
cards.subtitle: Viola riviniana
cards.description: Viola riviniana, the common dog-violet, is a species of flowering plant in the family Violaceae, native to Eurasia and Africa. It is also called wood violet and dog violet. It inhabits woodland edges, grassland and shady hedge banks.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Fabien Piednoir, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Fabien Piednoir

cards.name: Smooth Cat's Ear
cards.subtitle: Hypochaeris glabra
cards.description: Hypochaeris glabra is a species of flowering plant in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae known by the common name smooth cat's ear. It is native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East but it can be found on other continents where it is an introduced species and a widespread weed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Heart-leaf Ice Plant
cards.subtitle: Mesembryanthemum cordifolium
cards.description: Mesembryanthemum cordifolium, formerly known as Aptenia cordifolia, is a species of succulent plant in the family Aizoaceae. It is a creeping plant that forms a carpet of flat-growing perennial herbs in groups on the ground from a base. The genus name means middle-embryo flower in reference to the position of the ovary in the flower.
cards.keyFeatures: This is a succulent, creeping, short-lived, mat-forming perennial herb growing in flat clumps on the ground from a woody base. Plants only rise to about 10 centimetres (3.9 in) tall but prostrate stems reach up to about 60 centimetres (24 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eric Knight, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Hairy Tare
cards.subtitle: Vicia hirsuta
cards.description: Vicia hirsuta (syn. Ervilia hirsuta) (hairy tare, hairy vetch, tiny vetch) is a species of flowering plant in the pea and bean family Fabaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an annual herb producing a slender, often four-sided, hairless to lightly hairy, climbing stem up to 70 to 90 centimeters tall, and known to well exceed one meter at times.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Common Thornapple
cards.subtitle: Datura stramonium
cards.description: Datura stramonium, known by the common names thornapple, jimsonweed (jimson weed) or stink blade, is a poisonous flowering plant in the Daturae tribe of the nightshade family Solanaceae. Its likely origin was in Central America, and it has been introduced in many world regions. It is an aggressive invasive weed in temperate climates and tropical climates across the world.
cards.keyFeatures: Datura stramonium is an erect, annual, freely branching herb that forms a bush 60 to 150 cm (2 to 5 ft) tall. The root is long, thick, fibrous, and white.
cards.imageCredit:
(c) 
Gero Brandenburg, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Hairy Hawkbit
cards.subtitle: Leontodon saxatilis
cards.description: Leontodon saxatilis is a species of hawkbit known by the common names lesser hawkbit, rough hawkbit, and hairy hawkbit. It is native to Europe and North Africa but can be found in many other places across the globe as an introduced species and often a noxious weed. This is a dandelion-like herb growing patches of many erect, leafless stems from a basal rosette of leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tamás Kiss, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tamás Kiss

cards.name: Caper Spurge
cards.subtitle: Euphorbia lathyris
cards.description: Euphorbia lathyris, the caper spurge or paper spurge, is a species of spurge native to Asia in western China, Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan and introduced elsewhere. Other names occasionally used include gopher spurge, gopher plant or mole plant.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Common Groundsel
cards.subtitle: Senecio vulgaris
cards.description: Senecio vulgaris, often known by the common names groundsel and old-man-in-the-spring, is a flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is an annual herb, native to the Palaearctic and widely naturalised as a ruderal species in suitable disturbed habitats worldwide.
cards.keyFeatures: Senecio vulgaris is an erect, herbaceous annual growing up to 40 centimetres (16 in) tall. The inflorescences usually lack ray florets and the yellow disc florets are mostly hidden by the bracts, giving the flowers an inconspicuous appearance.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Field Woundwort
cards.subtitle: Stachys arvensis
cards.description: Stachys arvensis is a species of flowering plant in the mint family known by the common names field woundwort and staggerweed. It is native to Europe, Western Asia, and North Africa. It is known on other continents as an introduced species and widespread weed.
cards.keyFeatures: Field woundwort is an annual herb with branched, square stems up to 45 cm long, growing with a sprawling or erect habit. The stems are pale green and covered with patent, sparsely glandular hairs up to 2 mm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Twiggy Mullein
cards.subtitle: Verbascum virgatum
cards.description: Verbascum virgatum, commonly known as twiggy mullein and wand mullein, is a plant species in the family Scrophulariaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a tall-growing biennial herb reaching a height of between 1 and 2 metres. The flowers are 3 to 4 cm in diameter and are yellow with a purple centre.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tomás Carranza Perales, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tomás Carranza Perales

cards.name: Great Mullein
cards.subtitle: Verbascum thapsus
cards.description: Verbascum thapsus, the great mullein, greater mullein or common mullein, is a species of mullein native to Europe, northern Africa, and Asia, and introduced in the Americas, Australia and New Zealand. It is a hairy biennial plant that can grow to 2 m tall or more. Its small, yellow flowers are densely grouped on a tall stem, which grows from a large rosette of leaves.
cards.keyFeatures: V. thapsus is a dicotyledonous plant that produces a rosette of leaves in its first year of growth. The leaves are large, up to 50 cm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Wendy McCrady, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Wendy McCrady

cards.name: Hairy Bittercress
cards.subtitle: Cardamine hirsuta
cards.description: Cardamine hirsuta, commonly called hairy bittercress, popping cress, common bittercress, hoary bittercress, hairy wood-cress, small bittercress, pepperweed, shotweed, or snapweed, is an annual or biennial species of plant in the family Brassicaceae, and is edible as a salad green. It is common in moist areas around the world.
cards.keyFeatures: Depending on the climate C. hirsuta may complete two generations in a year, one in the spring and one in the fall; also depending on the climate, the seeds may germinate in the fall and the plants may remain green throughout the winter before flowering in the spring.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Igor Balashov, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Igor Balashov

cards.name: Spider Plant
cards.subtitle: Chlorophytum comosum
