cards.description: Chlorophytum comosum, usually called spider plant or common spider plant due to its spider-like look, also known as spider ivy, airplane plant, ribbon plant (a name it shares with Dracaena sanderiana), and hen and chicks, is a species of evergreen perennial flowering plant of the family Asparagaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Chlorophytum comosum grows to about 60 cm (24 in) tall, although as a hanging plant it can descend many feet. It has fleshy, tuberous roots, each about 5–10 cm (2–4 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tom Fletcher, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tom Fletcher

cards.name: Prostrate Knotweed
cards.subtitle: Polygonum aviculare
cards.description: Polygonum aviculare or common knotgrass is a plant related to buckwheat and dock. It is also called prostrate knotweed, birdweed, pigweed and lowgrass. It is an annual found in fields and wasteland, with white flowers from June to October.
cards.keyFeatures: Common knotgrass is an annual, low-prostrate herb with semi-erect, branching stems, which forms patches up to about 2 m (6 ft 7 in) across as it matures. It has alternate linear-lanceolate leaves which are longer (7–15 mm (0.28–0.59 in)) on the main stems than on the branches (3–5 mm (0.12–0.20 in)).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dalgial, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Yellow Bitter-apple
cards.subtitle: Solanum linnaeanum
cards.description: Solanum linnaeanum is a nightshade species known as devil's apple and, in some places where it is introduced, apple of Sodom. The latter name is also used for other nightshades and entirely different plants elsewhere, in particular the poisonous milkweed Calotropis procera.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Pond Water-starwort
cards.subtitle: Callitriche stagnalis
cards.description: Callitriche stagnalis is a perennial aquatic vascular plant species. Also known as pond water-starwort, C. stagnalis, may thrive in a variety of aquatic and subaquatic habitats, specially those exhibiting slowly moving to non-moving water.
cards.imageCredit: (c) geosesarma, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by geosesarma

cards.name: Sweet Scabious
cards.subtitle: Sixalix atropurpurea
cards.description: Scabiosa atropurpurea (syn. Sixalix atropurpurea), the mourningbride, mournful widow, pincushion flower, or sweet scabious, is an ornamental plant of the genus Scabiosa in the family Caprifoliaceae. It is native to southern Europe.
cards.keyFeatures: Scabiosa atropurpurea has cauline leaves that are pinnately dissected, plants have red to purple flowers. It is native to southern Europe.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Great Willowherb
cards.subtitle: Epilobium hirsutum
cards.description: Epilobium hirsutum is a flowering plant belonging to the willowherb genus Epilobium in the family Onagraceae. It is commonly known as the great willowherb, great hairy willowherb or hairy willowherb. Local dialectal names include codlins and cream, apple pie and cherry pie.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a tall, perennial plant, reaching up to 2 metres in height. The robust stems are profusely hairy with soft spreading hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kai Löhr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kai Löhr

cards.name: Horehound
cards.subtitle: Marrubium vulgare
cards.description: Marrubium vulgare (white horehound or common horehound) is a flowering plant in the mint family (Lamiaceae), native to Europe, northern Africa, and southwestern and central Asia. Specifically, it emerged in the region between the Mediterranean Sea and Central Asia and now inhabits all continents save Antarctica. It is also widely naturalized in many places, including most of North and South America.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eugene Zelenko, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Red Valerian
cards.subtitle: Centranthus ruber
cards.description: Valeriana rubra (synonym Centranthus ruber), the red valerian, spur valerian, kiss-me-quick, fox's brush, devil's beard or Jupiter's beard, is a popular garden plant grown for its ornamental flowers. It is not to be confused with the closely related Valeriana officinalis (the garden valerian).
cards.keyFeatures: Valeriana rubra is a multi-stemmed perennial herbaceous plant up to 80 cm (31 in) tall with red, pink or white flowers. The leaves are generally 5–10 cm (2.0–3.9 in) long, the stem leaves being sessile and branch leaves sometimes having a petiole up to 5 cm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Marie-Lan Nguyen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Shamrock Oxalis
cards.subtitle: Oxalis articulata
cards.description: Oxalis articulata, known as pink-sorrel, pink wood sorrel, windowbox wood-sorrel, sourgrass, is a perennial species of flowering plant in the genus Oxalis native to Northern Argentina, Southern Brazil and Uruguay. It has been introduced in Europe in gardens and is now naturalized in these areas. The plant is susceptible to rust (disease due to the fungus Puccinia oxalidis).
cards.keyFeatures: As the name would imply, this species of Oxalis typically has pink to violet flowers with petals 10–15 mm long. Numerous tufted leaves emerge from the ground in a rosette.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gianni Del Bufalo bygdb, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Gianni Del Bufalo bygdb

cards.name: Greater Bird's-foot-trefoil
cards.subtitle: Lotus pedunculatus
cards.description: Lotus pedunculatus (formerly Lotus uliginosus), the big trefoil, greater bird's-foot-trefoil or marsh bird's-foot trefoil, is a member of the pea family (Fabaceae). It is a herbaceous perennial growing throughout Europe in damp, open locations.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Daniel Cahen, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniel Cahen

cards.name: Hairy Bird's-foot-trefoil
cards.subtitle: Lotus subbiflorus
cards.description: Lotus subbiflorus, the hairy bird's-foot trefoil, is a flowering plant of the pea family Fabaceae. It is a finely hairy annual plant, growing in dry, sandy ground, often near the sea, and producing sprawling stems with clusters of two to four lemon-yellow pea-type flowers, often with some borne inverted.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Wild Teasel
cards.subtitle: Dipsacus fullonum
cards.description: Dipsacus fullonum, syn. Dipsacus sylvestris, is a species of flowering plant known by the common names wild teasel or fuller's teasel, although the latter name is usually applied to the cultivated variety D. fullonum var. sativus. It is native to Eurasia and North Africa, but it is known in the Americas, southern Africa, Australia and New Zealand as an introduced species.
cards.keyFeatures: Teasels are easily identified with their prickly stem and leaves, and the inflorescence of purple, dark pink or lavender flowers that form a head on the end of the stem(s). The inflorescence is ovoid, 4–10 centimetres (1.6–3.9 in) long and 3–5 centimetres (1.2–2.0 in) broad, with a basal whorl of spiny bracts.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andreas Rockstein, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Mediterranean Stork's-bill
cards.subtitle: Erodium botrys
cards.description: Erodium botrys is a species of flowering plant in the geranium family known by the common names longbeak stork's bill, Mediterranean stork's-bill and broadleaf filaree.
cards.keyFeatures: Erodium botrys starts from a flat rosette of highly lobed green leaves on red petioles. It grows to heights of anywhere from 10 to 90 centimeters (3.9 to 35.4 in) with somewhat hairy stems and foliage.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Patricio Novoa Quezada, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: European Searocket
cards.subtitle: Cakile maritima
cards.description: Cakile maritima, sea rocket (Britain and Ireland) or European searocket (North America), is a common plant in the mustard family Brassicaceae. It is widespread in Europe, North Africa and western Asia, especially on coastlines. It can now be found in many other areas of the world where it has been introduced.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a glabrous, succulent annual, with a slender or stout taproot. It has a branched stem which is prostrate or ascending, growing up to 15–45 cm (5.9–17.7 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jürgen Howaldt, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Thread Iris
cards.subtitle: Moraea setifolia
cards.description: Moraea setifolia is a plant species in the family Iridaceae.
cards.imageCredit: (c) safiyyah hattas, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by safiyyah hattas

cards.name: Jersey Toadflax
cards.subtitle: Linaria pelisseriana
cards.description: Recorded 98 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Daniel Cahen, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniel Cahen

cards.name: Spanish Bluebell
cards.subtitle: Hyacinthoides hispanica
cards.description: Hyacinthoides hispanica (syn. Endymion hispanicus or Scilla hispanica), the Spanish bluebell or wood hyacinth, is a spring-flowering bulbous perennial native to the Iberian Peninsula.
cards.keyFeatures: It is distinguished from the common bluebell by its larger, paler, less pendulous blue flowers which do not all droop to one side like the common bluebell; a more erect flower stem (raceme); broader leaves; blue anthers (where the common bluebell has creamy-white ones); and little or no scent, unlike the strong fragrance of the northern species.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Mark Gurney, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Mark Gurney

cards.name: Variegated Thistle
cards.subtitle: Silybum marianum
cards.description: Silybum marianum is a species of thistle. It has various common names including milk thistle, blessed milkthistle, Marian thistle, Mary thistle, Saint Mary's thistle, Mediterranean milk thistle, variegated thistle and Scotch thistle (not to be confused with Onopordum acanthium or Cirsium vulgare). This species is an annual or biennial plant of the family Asteraceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Milk thistle is an upright herb that can grow to be 30 to 200 cm (12 to 79 in) tall and has an overall conical shape. The approximate maximum base diameter is 160 cm (63 in).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Kashmir Balsam
cards.subtitle: Impatiens balfourii
cards.description: Impatiens balfourii is a species of the genus Impatiens known by the common names Balfour's touch-me-not, Kashmir balsam, and poor man's orchid. It belongs to the family Balsaminaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: This is an annual herb growing 15–120 centimetres (5.9–47.2 in) in height. Its stem is glabrous, reddish, lined and very branched.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Common Peppercress
cards.subtitle: Lepidium africanum
cards.description: Lepidium africanum is a species of flowering plant belonging to the family Brassicaceae. It is an annual or perennial which ranges from Saudi Arabia and Sudan to southern Africa.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Ecroyd, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Ecroyd

cards.name: Black Medick
cards.subtitle: Medicago lupulina
cards.description: Medicago lupulina, commonly known as black medick, nonesuch, or hop clover, is a plant of dry grassland belonging to Fabaceae, the legume or clover family. It is native to Africa and Eurasia, and has been naturalized elsewhere.
cards.keyFeatures: Medicago lupulina is an annual or short-lived perennial plant, growing each year from adventitious buds on the roots. Mature plants measure from 15 to 80 centimetres (6 to 31 in) in height, with fine stems often lying flat at the beginning of growth and later erecting.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Smooth Hawksbeard
cards.subtitle: Crepis capillaris
cards.description: Crepis capillaris, the smooth hawksbeard, is a species of flowering plant in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae, and is native to Europe. It has become naturalized in other lands and is regarded as a weed in some places.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Small-flowered Onion Grass
cards.subtitle: Romulea minutiflora
cards.description: Recorded 92 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alice Shanks, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alice Shanks

cards.name: Cobbler's Pegs
cards.subtitle: Bidens pilosa
cards.description: Bidens pilosa is an annual species of herbaceous flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae. Its many common names include hitch hikers, black-jack, beggarticks, farmer's friends and Spanish needle, but most commonly referred to as cobblers pegs.
cards.keyFeatures: Bidens pilosa is a branched annual forb of gracile habit, growing up to 1.8 meters (5 ft 11 in) tall. It grows aggressively on disturbed land and often becomes weedy.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Bathurst Burr
cards.subtitle: Xanthium spinosum
cards.description: Xanthium spinosum (also known as Acanthoxanthium spinosum) is a species of flowering plant in the aster family known by many common names, including spiny cocklebur, prickly burweed and Bathurst burr. This species is part of the genus Xanthium that encompasses 25 different species of flowering plants of the daisy family, Asteraceae, and sunflower tribe.
cards.keyFeatures: Xanthium spinosum is an upright, highly branched, dichotomous, annual herb producing a slender stem up to 1 metre (3 ft 3 in) tall or slightly taller. It is lined at intervals with very long, sharp, yellowish, three pronged spines which may exceed three centimeters in length.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Antonio W. Salas, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Antonio W. Salas

cards.name: Brazilian Woodsorrel
cards.subtitle: Oxalis brasiliensis
cards.description: Oxalis brasiliensis, also known by its common name Brazilian woodsorrel is a species from the section Ionoxalis. It was first described by Dámaso Antonio Larrañaga.
cards.keyFeatures: Oxalis brasiliensis is a herbaceous, perennial plant with a very long but simple root and very small stems. It has yellow or brilliant crimson-purple flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Laura Clark, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Laura Clark

cards.name: Canary Island Palm
cards.subtitle: Phoenix canariensis
cards.description: Phoenix canariensis, the Canary Island date palm, is a species of flowering plant in the palm family Arecaceae, native to the Canary Islands off the coast of Northwestern Africa. It is a relative of Phoenix dactylifera, the true date palm. It is the natural symbol of the Canary Islands, together with the canary Serinus canaria.
cards.keyFeatures: Phoenix canariensis is a large, solitary palm, 10–20 m (33–66 ft) tall, the tallest recorded being 36 m (118 ft) tall. The leaves are pinnate, 4–6 m (13–20 ft) long, with 80–100 leaflets on each side of the central rachis.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jesús Cabrera, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Castor Bean
cards.subtitle: Ricinus communis
cards.description: Ricinus communis, the castor bean or castor oil plant, is a species of perennial flowering plant in the spurge family, Euphorbiaceae. It is the sole species in the monotypic genus, Ricinus, and subtribe, Ricininae. Its seed is the castor bean, which despite the term is not a bean (as it is not the seed of a member of the family Fabaceae).
cards.keyFeatures: Ricinus communis can vary greatly in its growth habit and appearance. The variability has been increased by breeders who have selected a range of cultivars for leaf and flower colours, and for oil production.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by natalie

cards.name: Clustered Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium glomeratum
cards.description: Trifolium glomeratum is a species of clover known by the common names clustered clover and bush clover.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an annual herb growing decumbent to upright in form with mostly hairless herbage. The leaves are made up of oval leaflets up to 1.2 centimeters (1⁄2 in) in length.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ken-ichi Ueda, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ken-ichi Ueda

cards.name: Bog Yellowcress
cards.subtitle: Rorippa palustris
cards.description: Rorippa palustris, marsh yellow-cress, bog yellow-cress or common yellow-cress, is a species of flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae. It is widespread and native to parts of Africa, and much of Asia, Europe and Eurasia, North America and the Caribbean. It can also be found in other parts of the world as an introduced species and a common weed, for example, in Australia and South America.
cards.keyFeatures: It produces an erect stem, sometimes with branches, attaining a maximum height of just over one meter. The leaves are up to 30 centimeters long and have toothed to deeply lobed edges.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Нурхайдарова Татьяна, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Нурхайдарова Татьяна

cards.name: False Grass-poly
cards.subtitle: Lythrum junceum
cards.description: Lythrum junceum is a species of perennial herb in the family Lythraceae native to the Mediterranean Basin, West Asia and Macaronesia. They have a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves. They are associated with freshwater habitat.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Daniela Costa, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniela Costa

cards.name: Sea Fig
cards.subtitle: Carpobrotus edulis
cards.description: Carpobrotus edulis is a creeping plant with succulent leaves in the fig-marigold family Aizoaceae, native to South Africa. Its common names include hottentot-fig, sour fig, ice plant, highway ice plant, or vygie.
cards.keyFeatures: Carpobrotus edulis is a creeping, mat-forming succulent species. It grows year round, with individual shoot segments growing more than 1 m (3 ft) per year.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alvesgaspar, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Fat Hen
cards.subtitle: Chenopodium album
cards.description: Chenopodium album is a fast-growing annual plant in the flowering plant family Amaranthaceae. Though cultivated in some regions, the plant is elsewhere considered a weed. Common names include lamb's quarters, melde, goosefoot, wild spinach and fat-hen, though several are also applied to other species of the genus Chenopodium, for which reason it is often distinguished as white goosefoot.
cards.keyFeatures: It tends to grow upright at first, reaching heights of 10–150 centimetres (4–59 in), rarely to 3 m; it then typically becomes recumbent after flowering (due to the weight of the foliage and seeds) unless supported by other plants. The leaves are alternate and varied in appearance.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Patrick Hacker, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Patrick Hacker

cards.name: Strawberry Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium fragiferum
cards.description: Trifolium fragiferum, the strawberry clover, is a herbaceous perennial plant species in the bean family Fabaceae. The species is native to Eurasia and parts of Africa. It is present in other places, such as sections of North America, as an introduced species.
cards.keyFeatures: Strawberry clover is a perennial herb with tough roots. It typically grows about 10 centimetres (4 in) tall but the much-branched stems can reach 40 cm (16 in) in length, rooting at the nodes to form patches up to 80 cm (31 in) across.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Darwin's Barberry
cards.subtitle: Berberis darwinii
cards.description: Berberis darwinii, Darwin's barberry, is a species of flowering plant in the family Berberidaceae. It is native to southern Chile and Argentina and naturalized elsewhere. Regional vernacular names include michay, calafate, and quelung.
cards.keyFeatures: Berberis darwinii has dense branches from ground level. The leaves are small oval, 12–25 mm (0.47–0.98 in) long and 5–12 mm (0.20–0.47 in) broad, with a spiny margin; they are borne in clusters of 2–5 together, subtended by a three-branched spine 2–4 mm long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: South African Daisy
cards.subtitle: Senecio pterophorus
cards.description: Recorded 77 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacob Moore, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Pink Knotweed
cards.subtitle: Persicaria capitata
cards.description: Persicaria capitata, the pink-headed persicaria, pinkhead smartweed, pink knotweed, Japanese knotweed, or pink bubble persicaria, is an Asian species of plants in the genus Persicaria within the Polygonaceae (US: buckwheat) family. It is native to Asia (China, South Asia, Indochina) and grown as an ornamental in other countries.
cards.keyFeatures: Persicaria capitata is a prostrate herb. The leaves are 1–6 cm long, 0.7–3 cm wide with pink to red bands or blotches and short scattered hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Forest and Kim Starr, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Kerkei
cards.subtitle: Crassula tetragona
cards.description: Crassula tetragona is a succulent plant native to Southern Africa. It is widely distributed from the Orange River boundary of Namaqualand to beyond the Kei River in the Eastern Cape. "Tetragona" comes from the phyllotaxy of the leaves. It is popularly named the "miniature pine tree" among ornamental plant enthusiasts, for its popular use as a "pine tree" in Bonsai.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is erect or spreads shrubless to 1 m (3 ft). It has woody stems with brown bark, with crossed pairs of leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Long-headed Poppy
cards.subtitle: Papaver dubium
cards.description: Papaver dubium is a species of poppy known by the common names long-headed poppy and blindeyes. It is an annual species which prefers sandy soils without lime. It is native to Europe, North Africa and south-western Asia and widespread as an introduction in America and elsewhere.
cards.keyFeatures: Papaver dubium is a variable annual, growing to about 60 cm (24 in) in height. It generally flowers in late spring to mid-summer.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Pink Jasmine
cards.subtitle: Jasminum polyanthum
cards.description: Jasminum polyanthum (Chinese: 多花素馨; pinyin: Duōhuāsùxīn), the many-flowered jasmine, pink jasmine, or white jasmine, is a species of flowering plant in the olive family Oleaceae, native to China and Myanmar. A strong evergreen twining climber, it is especially noted for its abundant, highly fragrant pink to white flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: When supported, the plant can grow up to 6 metres (20 feet) in height. The compound leaves with 5 to 9 leaflets are dark green on the upper surface and a lighter green beneath, with glabrous, terete or angular branches.
cards.imageCredit: (c) KENPEI, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Sweet Alyssum
cards.subtitle: Lobularia maritima
cards.description: Lobularia maritima (syn. Alyssum maritimum) is a species of low-growing flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae. Its common name is sweet alyssum or sweet Alison, also commonly referred to as just alyssum (from the genus Alyssum in which it was formerly classified).
cards.keyFeatures: Lobularia maritima is an annual plant (rarely a short-lived perennial plant) growing to 5–30 cm (2–12 in) tall by 20–30 cm (8–12 in) broad. The stem is very branched, with dense clusters of small flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Юрий Данилевский (Yuriy Danilevsky), some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Юрий Данилевский (Yuriy Danilevsky)

cards.name: Borage
cards.subtitle: Borago officinalis
cards.description: Borage ( or; Borago officinalis), also known as starflower, is an annual herb in the flowering plant family Boraginaceae native to the Mediterranean region. Although the plant contains small amounts of pyrrolizidine alkaloids, some parts are edible and its seeds provide oil.
cards.keyFeatures: B. officinalis grows to a height of 60 centimetres (2 feet), and is bristly or hairy all over the stems and leaves; the leaves are alternate, simple, and 5–15 cm (2–6 inches) long. The flowers are complete, perfect with five narrow, triangular-pointed petals.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eleftherios Katsillis, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eleftherios Katsillis

cards.name: American Black Nightshade
cards.subtitle: Solanum americanum
cards.description: Solanum americanum, commonly known as American black nightshade, small-flowered nightshade or glossy nightshade, is a herbaceous flowering plant.
cards.keyFeatures: Solanum americanum grows up to 1–1.5 metres (39–59 in) tall and is an annual or short-lived perennial. The leaves are alternate on the branch, and vary greatly in size, up to 10 centimetres (4 in) long and 7 cm (3 in) broad, with a 4 cm (1+1⁄2 in) petiole and a coarsely wavy or toothed margin.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cricket Raspet, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cricket Raspet

cards.name: Creeping Groundsel
cards.subtitle: Senecio angulatus
cards.description: Senecio angulatus, also known as creeping groundsel and Cape ivy, is a succulent flowering plant in the family Asteraceae that is native to South Africa. Cape ivy is a scrambling herb that can become an aggressive weed once established, making it an invasive species. It is grown as an ornamental plant for its satiny foliage and sweet-scented flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Field Madder
cards.subtitle: Sherardia arvensis
cards.description: Sherardia is a monotypic genus of flowering plants in the family Rubiaceae. The genus contains only one species, Sherardia arvensis, the (blue) field madder, which is widespread across most of Europe and northern Africa as well as southwest and central Asia (from Turkey to Saudi Arabia to Kazakhstan) and Macaronesia (Canary Islands, Azores, Madeira, Savage Islands).
cards.keyFeatures: Sherardia arvensis is an annual plant with trailing and upright stems growing up to 40 cm (16 in) long, having a square cross-section. The rough pointed bristly leaves of about 1 cm (0.39 in) in length are in whorls of four to six (normally six at the ends of the shoots, but four nearer the root).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gilles San Martin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Gilles San Martin

cards.name: Grape Groundcherry
cards.subtitle: Physalis viscosa
cards.description: Physalis viscosa is a species of flowering plant in the nightshade family known by many common names, including starhair groundcherry, stellate ground-cherry and grape groundcherry in English, and arrebenta-cavalo, balãozinho, and camambú in Portuguese and Spanish (from Guaraní akamambu, «blister»). It is native to South America, and it is known on other continents as an introduced species and sometimes a weed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Harlequin Flower
cards.subtitle: Sparaxis tricolor
cards.description: Sparaxis tricolor, known by the common names wandflower, harlequin flower, and sparaxis, is a bulb-forming perennial plant that grows in well-drained sunny soil. It gained its name from its colorful flowers which are bi- or tri-coloured with a golden centre and a small ring of brown surrounded by another colour.
cards.imageCredit: (c) LJ Moore-McClelland, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by LJ Moore-McClelland

cards.name: Slender Thistle
cards.subtitle: Carduus pycnocephalus
cards.description: Carduus pycnocephalus, with common names including Italian thistle, Italian plumeless thistle, and Plymouth thistle, is a species of thistle. It is native to the Mediterranean region in southern Europe, North Africa, and Western Asia; Eastern Europe and the Caucasus; and the Indian subcontinent.
cards.keyFeatures: A winter annual, Carduus pycnocephalus has stems ranging from 8 inches (20 cm) to 6.6 feet (2.0 m), glabrous to slightly wooly. The multiple stems are winged with spines.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Don Loarie, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Don Loarie

cards.name: Greater Herb Robert
cards.subtitle: Geranium yeoi
cards.description: Recorded 67 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cricket Raspet, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cricket Raspet

cards.name: Annual Saltmarsh Aster
cards.subtitle: Symphyotrichum subulatum
cards.description: Symphyotrichum subulatum (formerly Aster subulatus), commonly known as eastern annual saltmarsh aster or, in Britain and Ireland where it is naturalized, annual saltmarsh aster, is an annual plant in the family Asteraceae native to the eastern United States and the Gulf Coast to Texas. The species grows primarily in coastal salt marshes, although in the Ozarks it occurs as a non-marine weedy variety.
cards.keyFeatures: Symphyotrichum subulatum is an annual forb that possesses a single erect stem that can reach up to 1 meter (3 feet 3 inches) in height. The stem, along with its thin green to dark green leaves, are both hairless.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Red Bartsia
cards.subtitle: Parentucellia latifolia
cards.description: Parentucellia latifolia is a species of flowering plant in the family Orobanchaceae known by several common names, including red bartsia, red tarweed, and broadleaf glandweed. It is native to Europe, but it can be found on other continents, including Australia, as an introduced species. This is an erect annual herb producing a stiff, slender stem coated in hairs and sticky glands.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Saltmarsh Aster
cards.subtitle: Symphyotrichum squamatum
cards.description: Symphyotrichum subulatum (formerly Aster subulatus), commonly known as eastern annual saltmarsh aster or, in Britain and Ireland where it is naturalized, annual saltmarsh aster, is an annual plant in the family Asteraceae native to the eastern United States and the Gulf Coast to Texas. The species grows primarily in coastal salt marshes, although in the Ozarks it occurs as a non-marine weedy variety.
cards.keyFeatures: Symphyotrichum subulatum is an annual forb that possesses a single erect stem that can reach up to 1 meter (3 feet 3 inches) in height. The stem, along with its thin green to dark green leaves, are both hairless.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jared Shorma, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Creeping Woodsorrel
cards.subtitle: Oxalis corniculata
cards.description: Oxalis corniculata, the creeping woodsorrel, procumbent yellow sorrel or sleeping beauty, is a somewhat delicate-appearing, low-growing herbaceous plant in the family Oxalidaceae. Oxalis corniculata is a small creeping type of woodsorrel that tends to grow well in moist climates. It resembles the common yellow woodsorrel, Oxalis stricta.
cards.keyFeatures: It has a narrow, creeping stem that easily takes root at the nodes. Its trifoliate leaves are subdivided into three rounded leaflets, resembling a clover.
cards.imageCredit: (c) jacinta lluch valero, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Ground Asparagus
cards.subtitle: Asparagus aethiopicus
cards.description: Asparagus aethiopicus, Sprenger's asparagus, is a plant native to the Cape Provinces and the Northern Provinces of South Africa. Often used as an ornamental plant, it is considered an invasive weed in many locations. Asparagus fern, asparagus grass and foxtail fern are common names; however, it is unrelated to true ferns.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Two-leaved Cape Tulip
cards.subtitle: Moraea miniata
cards.description: Moraea miniata is a plant species in the family Iridaceae.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Bunch-flowered Daffodil
cards.subtitle: Narcissus tazetta
cards.description: Narcissus tazetta (paperwhite, bunch-flowered narcissus, bunch-flowered daffodil, Chinese sacred lily, cream narcissus, joss flower, polyanthus narcissus) is a perennial ornamental plant that grows from a bulb. Cultivars of N. tazetta include 'Caniculatus', 'Grand Soleil d'Or' and 'Ziva', which are popularly used for forcing indoors, as is the form of N. tazetta known as Chinese Sacred Lily.
cards.keyFeatures: Narcissus tazetta is amongst the tallest of the narcissi, and can grow to a height of up to 80 centimetres (31 in), with thin, flat leaves up to 40 centimetres (16 in) long and 15 millimetres (0.59 in) wide. Umbels have as many as 8 flowers, white with a yellow corona.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Francesco Santoro, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Francesco Santoro

cards.name: Parrot's Feather
cards.subtitle: Myriophyllum aquaticum
cards.description: Myriophyllum aquaticum is a flowering plant, a vascular dicot, commonly called parrot's-feather and parrot feather watermilfoil.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by 葉子

cards.name: Bitter Lettuce
cards.subtitle: Lactuca virosa
cards.description: Lactuca virosa is a plant in the Lactuca (lettuce) genus, often ingested for its mild analgesic and sedative effects. It is related to common lettuce (L. sativa), and is often called wild lettuce, bitter lettuce, laitue vireuse, opium lettuce, poisonous lettuce, tall lettuce, great lettuce or rakutu-karyumu-so.
cards.keyFeatures: Lactuca virosa is biennial, similar to prickly lettuce Lactuca serriola but taller – it can grow to 200 cm (80 inches or almost 7 feet). It is also stouter, the stem and leaves are more purple flushed, and the leaves are less divided, but more spreading, similarly to Mycelis muralis but showing more than 5 florets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andreas Rockstein, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Soap Aloe
cards.subtitle: Aloe maculata
cards.description: Aloe maculata (syn. Aloe saponaria), the soap aloe or zebra aloe, is a Southern African species of aloe. Local people in South Africa know it informally as the Bontaalwyn in Afrikaans, or lekhala in the Sesotho language.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a very variable species and hybridizes easily with other similar aloes, sometimes making it difficult to identify. The leaves range in colour from red to green, but always have distinctive "H-shaped" spots.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Vilseskogen, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Vilseskogen

cards.name: Watercress
cards.subtitle: Nasturtium officinale
cards.description: Watercress or yellowcress (Nasturtium officinale) is a species of aquatic flowering plant in the cabbage family, Brassicaceae. Watercress is a rapidly growing perennial plant native to Eurasia. It is one of the oldest known leaf vegetables consumed by humans.
cards.keyFeatures: Watercress can grow up to 60 centimetres (24 in) in length. The stems are hollow and float in water.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Tree, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Tree

cards.name: Canada Thistle
cards.subtitle: Cirsium arvense
cards.description: Cirsium arvense is a perennial species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae, native throughout Europe and western Asia, northern Africa and widely introduced elsewhere. The standard English name in its native area is creeping thistle. It is also commonly misnomered as Canada thistle and sometimes as field thistle.
cards.keyFeatures: Cirsium arvense is a C3 carbon fixation plant. The C3 plants originated during Mesozoic and Paleozoic eras, and tend to thrive in areas where sunlight intensity is moderate, temperatures are moderate, and ground water is plentiful.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Matt Lavin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Purple Foxglove
cards.subtitle: Digitalis purpurea
cards.description: Digitalis purpurea, the foxglove or common foxglove, is a toxic species of flowering plant in the plantain family Plantaginaceae, native to and widespread throughout most of temperate Europe. It has also naturalized in parts of North America, as well as some other temperate regions. The plant is a popular garden subject, with many cultivars available.
cards.keyFeatures: Digitalis purpurea is an herbaceous biennial or short-lived perennial plant. The leaves are spirally arranged, simple, 10–35 cm (4–14 in) long and 5–12 cm (2–5 in) broad, and are covered with gray-white pubescent and glandular hairs, imparting a woolly texture.
cards.imageCredit: (c) nbasargin, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Wild Clary
cards.subtitle: Salvia verbenaca
cards.description: Salvia verbenaca, also known as wild clary or wild sage, is native to the British Isles, the Mediterranean region in Southern Europe, North Africa, and Near East, and in the Caucasus. It can be found as an introduced species that has naturalized in many parts of the world, including the eastern United States, California, Mexico, Argentina, Uruguay, southern Africa, Australia, New Zealand and China.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Emanuele Santarelli, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Emanuele Santarelli

cards.name: Field Bindweed
cards.subtitle: Convolvulus arvensis
cards.description: Convolvulus arvensis, or field bindweed, is a species of bindweed in the Convolvulaceae native to Europe and Asia. It is a rhizomatous and climbing or creeping herbaceous perennial plant with stems growing to 0.5–2 metres (1.6–6.6 ft) in length. It is usually found at ground level with small white and pink flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Convolvulus arvensis is a perennial vine that typically climbs to 1 metre (3.3 ft). The vine produces woody rhizomes from which it resprouts in the spring, or when the aboveground vines are removed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Cretan Mallow
cards.subtitle: Malva multiflora
cards.description: Malva multiflora (previously known as Lavatera cretica) is a species of flowering plant in the mallow family known by the common names Cornish mallow and Cretan hollyhock. It is native to western Europe, North Africa, and the Mediterranean Basin, and it is naturalized in areas with a Mediterranean climate, such as parts of Australia, South Africa, and California.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Lesser Swine-cress
cards.subtitle: Lepidium didymum
cards.description: Lepidium didymum, the lesser swine-cress, is a species of flowering plant in the family Brassicaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: Lepidium didymum is an annual or biennial herb with decumbent or ascending and glabrous green stems, up to 40 centimetres (16 in) long, radiating from a central position. The leaves are pinnate and alternate and can reach a length of 5 cm (2 in).
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jesse Rorabaugh

cards.name: Squashed Sorrel
cards.subtitle: Oxalis compressa
cards.description: Recorded 57 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jared Shorma, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Garden Pink-sorrel
cards.subtitle: Oxalis latifolia
cards.description: Oxalis latifolia is a species of flowering plant in the woodsorrel family known by the common names garden pink-sorrel and broadleaf woodsorrel. It is native to Mexico and parts of Central and South America. However, it has propagated to other parts of the world.
cards.keyFeatures: This is a perennial herb growing from a system of small bulbs and spreading via stolons. There is no stem.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Squirting Cucumber
cards.subtitle: Ecballium elaterium
cards.description: Ecballium is a genus of flowering plants in the family Cucurbitaceae containing a single species, Ecballium elaterium, also called the squirting cucumber. Its unusual common name derives from the ripe fruit squirting a stream of mucilaginous liquid containing its seeds as a means of seed dispersal, an example of rapid plant movement.
cards.keyFeatures: Ecballium elaterium is a herbaceous perennial plant with a tuberous root, usually trailing on the ground but sometimes shrubby, with bristly stems. The leaves are lobed, greyish-green, and rough-surfaced and bristly-hairy.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Daniel Cahen, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniel Cahen

cards.name: Chinese Mugwort
cards.subtitle: Artemisia verlotiorum
cards.description: Artemisia verlotiorum, the Chinese mugwort, is a species of plant in the sunflower family, widespread across much of Eurasia.
cards.keyFeatures: It has oblong reddish to brown capitula, its stems are green and the leaves broader, lighter colored and denser on the stem. The plant is more strongly and pleasantly aromatic than Artemisia vulgaris.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Smith, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bindyi
cards.subtitle: Soliva sessilis
cards.description: Soliva sessilis is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae. It is one of up to nine species of the genus Soliva and is a low-growing, herbaceous annual plant. Its common names include field burrweed, Onehunga-weed, lawn burrweed, lawnweed, jo-jo weed and common soliva.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Slender Centaury
cards.subtitle: Centaurium tenuiflorum
cards.description: Centaurium tenuiflorum, the slender centaury, is a species of annual herb in the family Gentianaceae. They have a self-supporting growth form and simple, broad leaves. Individuals can grow to 17 cm tall.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Crap Fou, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Crap Fou

cards.name: Pig's Ear
cards.subtitle: Cotyledon orbiculata
cards.description: Cotyledon orbiculata, commonly known as pig's ear or round-leafed navel-wort, is a South African succulent plant belonging to the genus Cotyledon.
cards.keyFeatures: Cotyledon orbiculata is an extremely variable species, one that grows to approximately 1.3 m (4.3 ft) in height. It has gray-green leaves (up to 13 by 7 cm (5.1 by 2.8 in)), which naturally develop a white, powdery substance (known as farina) on their surfaces; this farina helps reflect sunlight and conserve water.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Roderick Cameron, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Roderick Cameron

cards.name: Marsh Parsley
cards.subtitle: Cyclospermum leptophyllum
cards.description: Cyclospermum leptophyllum (also, Ciclospermum l.) is a species of plant in the family Apiaceae known by the common names marsh parsley, slender celery and fir-leaved celery. This is a plant found worldwide at warm temperate to tropical latitudes and is considered a noxious weed in many areas. It is a taprooted branching herb reaching just over half a meter in height at maximum.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Blue Stars
cards.subtitle: Aristea ecklonii
cards.description: Aristea ecklonii (common names: blue flies, blue stars, blue-eyed iris, blue corn-lily) is a plant species in the Iridaceae, first described in 1866. It is native to central and southern Africa from South Africa north to Cameroon and Tanzania. The plant is an evergreen perennial with small, blue flowers, growing in clumps with upright, grass-like leaves 15–18 in (38–46 cm) in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Red Hot Poker
cards.subtitle: Kniphofia uvaria
cards.description: Kniphofia uvaria is a species of flowering plant in the family Asphodelaceae, commonly known as tritomea, torch lily, or red hot poker, due to the shape and color of its inflorescence. The leaves are reminiscent of a lily, and the flowerhead can reach up to 1.5 m (5 ft) in height. There are many varieties of torch lily, and they bloom at different times during the growing season.
cards.imageCredit: (c) magriet b, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by magriet b

cards.name: Yellow Flag Iris
cards.subtitle: Iris pseudacorus
cards.description: Iris pseudacorus, the yellow flag, yellow iris, or water flag, is a species of flowering plant in the family Iridaceae. It is native to Europe, western Asia and northwest Africa. Its specific epithet pseudacorus means "false acorus", referring to the similarity of its leaves to those of Acorus calamus (sweet flag), as they have a prominently veined mid-rib and sword-like shape.
cards.keyFeatures: This herbaceous flowering perennial plant grows to 100–150 cm (39–59 in), or a rare 2 m (6 ft 7 in) tall, with erect leaves up to 90 cm (35 in) long and 3 cm (1.2 in) broad. The flowers are bright yellow, 7–10 cm (2.8–3.9 in) across, with the typical iris form.
cards.imageCredit: (c) E. Borchert, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by E. Borchert

cards.name: Timwort
cards.subtitle: Cicendia quadrangularis
cards.description: Recorded 49 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Alex Heyman

cards.name: Heart-podded Hoary Cress
cards.subtitle: Lepidium draba
cards.description: Lepidium draba, commonly known as hoary cress, whitetop, whiteweed, or peppergrass, is a perennial plant species in the mustard family, Brassicaceae. It is native to Eurasia, specifically regions of Europe and western to central Asia, but has become widely distributed across the globe, including most of the United States, as well as in Canada and parts of Mexico.
cards.keyFeatures: Whitetop is a perennial herb that reproduces by seeds and by horizontal creeping roots. The stem is stoutish, erect or spreading, 10 to 80 centimetres (4 to 31+1⁄2 inches) tall, branched, covered sparsely with grayish, soft hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) joy russell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by joy russell

cards.name: Garden Lobelia
cards.subtitle: Lobelia erinus
cards.description: Lobelia erinus (edging lobelia, garden lobelia or trailing lobelia) is a species of flowering plant in the bellflower family Campanulaceae, native to southern Africa.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a low growing, prostrate or scrambling herbaceous perennial plant growing to 8–15 cm tall. The basal leaves are oval, 10 mm long and 4–8 mm broad, with a toothed margin; leaves higher on the stems are slender and sometimes untoothed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Alexis Tinker-Tsavalas

cards.name: Garden Parsley
cards.subtitle: Petroselinum crispum
cards.description: Parsley, or garden parsley (Petroselinum crispum), is a species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae that is native to Greece, the Balkans, Algeria and Morocco. It has been introduced and naturalized in Europe and elsewhere in the world with suitable climates, and is widely cultivated as a herb and a vegetable.
cards.keyFeatures: Garden parsley is a bright green, biennial plant in temperate climates, or an annual herb in subtropical and tropical areas. Where it grows as a biennial, in the first year, it forms a rosette of tripinnate leaves 10–25 cm (3.9–9.8 in) long with numerous 1–3 cm leaflets, and a taproot used as a food store over the winter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Vítor Jorge, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Vítor Jorge

cards.name: Tangier Pea
cards.subtitle: Lathyrus tingitanus
cards.description: Lathyrus tingitanus is a species of wild pea known by the common name Tangier pea. It is native to southwestern Europe and Northwest Africa, and it is present in other regions of the world as an introduced species, including the Pacific Northwest of the United States. This is an annual herb producing a winged stem which climbs by means of coiled tendrils.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bruce Calvert, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bruce Calvert

cards.name: Yellow Centaury
cards.subtitle: Cicendia filiformis
cards.description: Cicendia filiformis, also called yellow centaury or slender cicendia, is a species of flowering planet of the family Gentianaceae.
cards.keyFeatures: C. filiformis grows to 2–12 cm (0.8–4.7 in) in height with linear leaves 2–6 mm long. The flowers are yellow (but can be tinged with pink), have four petals and only open in sunlight.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Gilles San Martin, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Gilles San Martin

cards.name: Narrow-leaf Cotton Bush
cards.subtitle: Gomphocarpus fruticosus
cards.description: Gomphocarpus fruticosus (swan plant; narrow-leaved cotton bush) is a species of plant native to South Africa. It is also common in Australia and New Zealand where it is a host of the monarch butterfly. The plant's tissues contain sufficient cardenolides that consumption of significant quantities of the plant's leaves, stems, or fruit may lead to death in livestock and humans.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ann Bentley, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ann Bentley

cards.name: Eyebane
cards.subtitle: Euphorbia maculata
cards.description: Euphorbia maculata, known as spotted spurge, prostrate spurge (not to be confused with Euphorbia prostrata), milk purslane, or spotted sandmat, is a fast-growing annual plant in the family Euphorbiaceae. It is native to North America, where it is generally considered a common weed. It can be found in disturbed soils such as garden beds, along railroad tracks, and in the cracks of sidewalks.
cards.keyFeatures: As originally described in 1753 by Carl Linnaeus, Euphorbia maculata is an herbaceous plant with small, oblong opposite leaves. The leaves are pilose, or covered in small thin hairs, and generally have a crenate (scalloped) edge.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Douglas Goldman, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Douglas Goldman

cards.name: Hairypink
cards.subtitle: Petrorhagia dubia
cards.description: Petrorhagia dubia is a species of flowering plant in the family Caryophyllaceae known by the common name hairy pink. It is native to southern Europe and the Mediterranean Basin, but it is known on other continents, including Australia and North and South America, as an introduced species and sometimes a weed. It is an annual herb growing 25 to 60 centimeters tall, but known to reach 90 centimeters in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) David Fischer, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by David Fischer

cards.name: Tomato
cards.subtitle: Solanum lycopersicum
cards.description: The tomato (US:, UK:; Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable. The tomato is a member of the nightshade family that includes tobacco, potato, and chili peppers. It originated from western South America, and may have been domesticated there, in Mexico, or in Central America.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Baby's Tears
cards.subtitle: Soleirolia soleirolii
cards.description: Soleirolia soleirolii (, syn. Helxine soleirolii) is a flowering plant in the nettle family. It has a number of common names, including baby's tears, angel's tears, peace in the home, bits and pieces, bread and cheese, Corsican creeper, Corsican curse, friendship plant, mind-your-own-business, pollyanna vine, Paddy's wig, and mother of thousands.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a delicate-looking creeping herb with juicy bright green or yellow leaves and multitudes of tiny pink flowers, male and female separate. It grows close to the ground in mats and is sometimes used in ornamental gardens alongside ferns and other moisture-loving types of plant.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Carnat Joel, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Hedge Woundwort
cards.subtitle: Stachys sylvatica
cards.description: Stachys sylvatica, commonly known as hedge woundwort, whitespot, or sometimes as hedge nettle, is a perennial herbaceous plant growing to 80 cm (31 in) tall in woodland and unmanaged grassland. In temperate zones of the northern hemisphere it flowers in July and August. The flowers are purple.
cards.keyFeatures: Hedge woundwort is an erect perennial plant with slender underground runners. The stem branches occasionally and is squarish and hairy, with glandular hairs on the upper part of the plant.
cards.imageCredit:
(c) 
Ivar Leidus, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Cursed Crowfoot
cards.subtitle: Ranunculus sceleratus
cards.description: Ranunculus sceleratus known by the common names celery-leaved buttercup, celery-leaf buttercup, and cursed buttercup is a species of flowering plant in the buttercup family Ranunculaceae. It has a circumpolar distribution in the northern hemisphere, native to temperate and boreal North America and Eurasia, where it grows in wet and moist habitats, including ponds and streambanks.
cards.keyFeatures: Ranunculus sceleratus is an annual herb growing up to half a meter tall. The leaves are more or less glabrous (hairless) and have small blades each deeply lobed or divided into three leaflets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Brian Finzel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Brian Finzel

cards.name: Stinking Iris
cards.subtitle: Iris foetidissima
cards.description: Iris foetidissima, the stinking iris, gladdon, Gladwin iris, roast-beef plant, or stinking gladwin, is a species of flowering plant in the family Iridaceae, found in open woodland, hedgebanks and on sea-cliffs. Its natural range is Western Europe, including England (south of Durham) and also Ireland, and from France south and east to N. Africa, Italy and Greece.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Drepanostoma, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Drepanostoma

cards.name: Weed African Thistle
cards.subtitle: Berkheya rigida
cards.description: Recorded 42 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Julia Palmer, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Moth Mullein
cards.subtitle: Verbascum blattaria
cards.description: Verbascum blattaria, the moth mullein, is a flowering biennial plant belonging to the figwort family Scrophulariaceae. A native of Eurasia and North Africa, it has naturalized in the United States and most of Canada since its introduction and has become an invasive species there. It has been declared a noxious weed by the state of Colorado.
cards.keyFeatures: The moth mullein is a biennial plant. In its first year after sowing, its leaves develop as a basal rosette.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sandy Wolkenberg, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Sandy Wolkenberg

cards.name: Jerusalem Artichoke
cards.subtitle: Helianthus tuberosus
cards.description: The Jerusalem artichoke (Helianthus tuberosus), also called sunroot, sunchoke, wild sunflower, topinambur, or earth apple, is a species of sunflower native to central North America. It is cultivated widely across the temperate zone for its tuber, which is used as a root vegetable.
cards.keyFeatures: Helianthus tuberosus is a herbaceous perennial plant growing to 1.5–3 m (4 ft 11 in – 9 ft 10 in) tall with opposite leaves on the lower part of the stem but alternate towards the top. The leaves have a rough, hairy texture.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tero Laakso, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Four O'clock
cards.subtitle: Mirabilis jalapa
cards.description: Mirabilis jalapa, the marvel of Peru or four o'clock flower, is the most commonly grown ornamental species of Mirabilis plant, and is available in a range of colors. Mirabilis in Latin means wonderful and Jalapa (or Xalapa) is the state capital of Veracruz in Mexico. Mirabilis jalapa is believed to have been cultivated by the Aztecs for medicinal and ornamental purposes.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a perennial, herbaceous, bushy plant that reaches stature heights of mostly 1 meter, rarely up to 2 meters, in height. It may also be grown as an annual, especially in the temperate zone.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ricard Busquets Reverte, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ricard Busquets Reverte

cards.name: Common Broomrape
cards.subtitle: Orobanche minor
cards.description: Orobanche minor, the hellroot, common broomrape, lesser broomrape, small broomrape, broomrape minor or clover broomrape, is a holoparasitic flowering plant belonging to the family Orobanchaceae. It is one of about 150 non-photosynthetic plants in the genus Orobanche that parasitize autotrophic plants. It is a federally listed noxious weed in the United States.
cards.imageCredit: (c) David Whyte, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by David Whyte

cards.name: Sharp-leaved Fluellen
cards.subtitle: Kickxia elatine
cards.description: Kickxia elatine (commonly known as sharpleaf cancerwort and sharp-leaved fluellen) is a species of flowering plant in the family Plantaginaceae. It is native to Europe and Asia, but it is present on other continents as an introduced species, and sometimes a noxious weed.
cards.keyFeatures: This is a small hairy herb with a trailing stem with many branches. It produces oval to arrowhead-shaped fuzzy leaves at wide intervals along the slender stem, and solitary snapdragon-like spurred flowers borne on long, straight pedicels.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Soft Stork's-bill
cards.subtitle: Erodium malacoides
cards.description: Erodium malacoides is a species of flowering plant in the geranium family known by the common names mallow-leaved stork's bill, Mediterranean stork's bill, and soft stork's-bill. It is an annual or biennial herb which is native to the Mediterranean region in southern Europe (north to 49°N in western France), northern Africa, and southwest Asia. It can be found locally elsewhere is an introduced species.
cards.keyFeatures: The young plant grows a number of rugose green leaves, radially outward flat against the ground. The stems reach 10–60 cm in height, with more leaves on long, hairy petioles, with glandular hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: European Heliotrope
cards.subtitle: Heliotropium europaeum
cards.description: Heliotropium europaeum is a species of heliotrope known by the common names European heliotrope and European turn-sole.
cards.keyFeatures: Heliotropium europaeum is an annual herb growing from a taproot and reaching maximum heights near 40 centimeters (16 in). The stem and oval-shaped leaves are covered in soft hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) anonymous, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Upright Chickweed
cards.subtitle: Moenchia erecta
cards.description: Moenchia erecta, the erect chickweed or upright chickweed (though the latter name may refer to any species of Moenchia), is a small annual plant in the family Caryophyllaceae. It can grow to over 10 cm in height, but it is usually smaller. It has blue-green glaucous leaves, and small, delicate white flowers.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Elspeth Swan

cards.name: Two-seeded Vetch
cards.subtitle: Vicia disperma
cards.description: Recorded 39 times around Greater Melbourne on iNaturalist.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Saryu Mae 前 朝琉, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Saryu Mae 前 朝琉

cards.name: Kahili Ginger
cards.subtitle: Hedychium gardnerianum
cards.description: Hedychium gardnerianum, the Kahili ginger, Kahila garland-lily or ginger lily, is a species of flowering plant in the ginger family Zingiberaceae, native to the Himalayas in India, Nepal, and Bhutan. It is an erect herbaceous perennial growing to 8 ft (2.4 m) tall with long, bright green leaves clasping the tall stems. The very fragrant pale yellow and red flowers are held in dense spikes above the foliage.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Silverleaf Cotoneaster
cards.subtitle: Cotoneaster pannosus
cards.description: Cotoneaster pannosus is a species of Cotoneaster known by the common name silverleaf cotoneaster. This woody shrub is native to south central China but it has been introduced to other areas of the world, including southern Africa and Australia as an ornamental. It has become naturalized in some areas but it is a troublesome noxious weed in others, for example, in Hawaii.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Potato
cards.subtitle: Solanum tuberosum
cards.description: The potato () is a starchy tuberous vegetable native to the Americas that is consumed as a staple food in many parts of the world. Potatoes are underground stem tubers of the plant Solanum tuberosum, a perennial in the nightshade family Solanaceae. Wild potato species can be found from the southern United States to southern Chile.
cards.keyFeatures: Potato plants are herbaceous perennials that grow up to one metre (three feet) high. The stems are hairy.
cards.imageCredit: (c) jamie-aa, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by jamie-aa

cards.name: Fireweed
cards.subtitle: Senecio madagascariensis
cards.description: Senecio madagascariensis, also known as Madagascar ragwort, is a species of the genus Senecio and family Asteraceae that is native to Southern Africa. Other common names include Madagascar groundsel and fireweed. It has been included on the noxious weeds list for Hawaii and the reject list for Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: It is an erect, glabrous (smooth stemmed) herb that grows up to 20–60 cm in length. It may become woody and shrub-like in appropriate conditions.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lucas Rubio, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lucas Rubio

cards.name: Yellow Fortnight Lily
cards.subtitle: Dietes bicolor
cards.description: Dietes bicolor, the African iris, butterfly flag, fortnight lily, or peacock flower, is a clump-forming rhizomatous perennial plant with long sword-like evergreen pale green leaves, growing from multiple fans at the base of the clump. This species belongs to the iris family Iridaceae. It can form large clumps if left undisturbed for years.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Pot Marigold
cards.subtitle: Calendula officinalis
cards.description: Calendula officinalis, Mary's gold, common marigold, the pot marigold, Scotch marigold, or ruddles, is a flowering plant in the daisy family, Asteraceae. It is probably native to southern Europe, but its long history of cultivation makes its precise origin unknown, and it is widely naturalised. The florets are edible and the plant has historically been used as medicine.
cards.keyFeatures: Calendula officinalis is a short-lived aromatic herbaceous perennial, growing to 80 cm (31 in) tall, with sparsely branched lax or upright stems. The leaves are oblong-lanceolate, 5–17 cm (2–7 in) long, hairy on both sides, and with margins entire or occasionally waved or weakly toothed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Corin@ 2008, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: American Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Gamochaeta americana
cards.description: Gamochaeta americana, also known as American everlasting, is a plant in the family Asteraceae.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by kcthetc1

cards.name: Bull Mallow
cards.subtitle: Malva nicaeensis
cards.description: Malva nicaeensis is a species of flowering plant in the mallow family known by the common names bull mallow and French mallow. It grows up to 60 centimetres (24 in) tall, producing pinkish flowers. It grows in the Middle East, where it has variously served as food.
cards.keyFeatures: Malva nicaeensis is an annual or biennial herb producing a hairy, upright stem up to 60 centimetres (24 in) long. The leaves are up to 12 cm wide and have several slight lobes along the edges.
cards.imageCredit: (c) shira gal, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Century Plant
cards.subtitle: Agave americana
cards.description: Agave americana, commonly known as the century plant, maguey, or American aloe, is a flowering plant species belonging to the family Asparagaceae. It is native to Mexico and the United States.
cards.keyFeatures: The common name "century plant" stems from its monocarpic nature of flowering only once at the end of its long life. After flowering, the plant dies but produces adventitious shoots from the base, allowing its growth to continue.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Duarte Frade, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Duarte Frade

cards.name: Natal Lily
cards.subtitle: Clivia miniata
cards.description: Clivia miniata, the Natal lily or bush lily, is a species of flowering plant in the genus Clivia of the family Amaryllidaceae, native to woodland habitats in South Africa (Eastern Cape, Mpumalanga and KwaZulu-Natal provinces) and Eswatini. It is also widely cultivated as an ornamental.
cards.keyFeatures: Clivia miniata has a fleshy, mostly underground stem (rhizome) to 2 cm (1 in) in diameter, with numerous fleshy roots. The stem produces long, arching, strap-like leaves growing to about 45 cm (18 in) long, arranged in two opposing rows (distichous).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Blue Rock Bindweed
cards.subtitle: Convolvulus sabatius
cards.description: Convolvulus sabatius, the ground blue-convolvulus or blue rock bindweed, is a species of flowering plant in the family Convolvulaceae, native to Italy and North Africa, and often seen in cultivation.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a woody-stemmed trailing perennial plant, growing to 20 cm (8 in) in height. It has slightly hairy leaves and light blue to violet flowers, often with a lighter centre, which is 2.5–5 cm (1–2 in) in diameter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sophia K, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Sophia K

cards.name: Banana Passionfruit
cards.subtitle: Passiflora tarminiana
cards.description: Passiflora tarminiana (or banana passionfruit) is a species of passionfruit. The yellow fruits are edible and their resemblance to small, straight bananas has given it the name banana passionfruit in some countries. It is native to the uplands of tropical South America and is now cultivated in many countries.
cards.keyFeatures: Passiflora tarminiana is a high climbing vine with hairy stems and petioles. Where the petioles join the stem it has stipules which are 4–7 by 2–3 mm and are soon deciduous.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nathan Aaron, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Sea Spurge
cards.subtitle: Euphorbia paralias
cards.description: Euphorbia paralias, the sea spurge, is a species of flowering plant in the family Euphorbiaceae, native to Europe, northern Africa and western Asia. The species is widely naturalised in Australia. It invades coastal areas, displacing local species and colonising open sand areas favoured by certain nesting birds.
cards.keyFeatures: Euphorbia paralias is an erect, glaucous, perennial plant, growing up to 70 centimetres (28 in) tall. It has many stems, dividing into 3–5 fertile branches, each branching further.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Munster Mad

cards.name: Clockweed
cards.subtitle: Oenothera lindheimeri
cards.description: Oenothera lindheimeri, commonly known as Lindheimer's beeblossom, white gaura, pink gaura, Lindheimer's clockweed, and Indian feather, is a species of Oenothera. Several of its common names derive from the genus Gaura, in which this species was formerly placed. The perennial plant is native to southern Louisiana and Texas.
cards.keyFeatures: Oenothera lindheimeri is a perennial herbaceous plant growing to 50 to 150 centimeters (20–60 in) tall, with densely clustered branched stems growing from an underground rhizome. The leaves are finely hairy, lanceolate, 1 to 9 cm (1⁄2–3+1⁄2 in) long and 1 to 13 mm (1⁄16–1⁄2 in) broad, with a coarsely toothed margin.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Red Clover
cards.subtitle: Trifolium pratense
cards.description: Trifolium pratense (from Latin prātum, meaning meadow), red clover, is a herbaceous species of flowering plant in the bean family, Fabaceae. It is native to the Old World, but planted and naturalised in many other regions.
cards.keyFeatures: The red clover is a herbaceous, short-lived perennial plant, which is generally variable in size, growing to 20–80 cm (8–31 in) tall. It has a deep taproot which makes it tolerant to drought and gives it a good soil structuring effect.

cards.name: Clustered Dock
cards.subtitle: Rumex conglomeratus
cards.description: Rumex conglomeratus, known as clustered dock and sharp dock, is a plant of the family Polygonaceae. It is an annual or biennial plant growing up to 100 cm high. A native of Europe, Asia and North Africa, it has also been introduced into North America.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Piermario Maculan

cards.name: Common Grape Hyacinth
cards.subtitle: Muscari armeniacum
cards.description: Muscari armeniacum is a species of flowering plant in the squill subfamily Scilloideae of the asparagus family Asparagaceae (formerly the lilies, Liliaceae). It is a bulbous perennial with basal, simple leaves and short flowering stems. It is one of a number of species and genera known as grape hyacinth, in this case Armenian grape hyacinth or garden grape-hyacinth.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Patrick Hacker, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Patrick Hacker

cards.name: Opium Poppy
cards.subtitle: Papaver somniferum
cards.description: Papaver somniferum, commonly known as the opium poppy or breadseed poppy, is a species of flowering plant in the family Papaveraceae. It is the species of plant from which both opium and poppy seeds are derived and is also a valuable ornamental plant grown in gardens.
cards.keyFeatures: Papaver somniferum is an annual herb growing to about 100 centimetres (40 inches) tall. The plant is strongly glaucous, giving a greyish-green appearance, and the stem and leaves bear a sparse distribution of coarse hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) David Perez, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Fringed Willowherb
cards.subtitle: Epilobium ciliatum
cards.description: Epilobium ciliatum, known by the common names fringed willowherb, American willowherb, slender willow herb, and northern willow herb is a species of flowering plant in the willowherb family Onagraceae. This species is native to much of North America, southern South America, and East Asia. It is an introduced species in much of Eurasia and Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Epilobium ciliatum is a clumping perennial often exceeding 1.5 metres (5 ft) in height. It has thickly veined lance-shaped leaves which may be up to 15 centimeters long toward the base of the plant.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jon Sullivan

cards.name: Feverfew
cards.subtitle: Tanacetum parthenium
cards.description: Tanacetum parthenium, known as feverfew, is a flowering plant in the daisy family, Asteraceae. It may be grown as an ornament, and may be identified by its synonyms, Chrysanthemum parthenium and Pyrethrum parthenium. Having its origin in the Balkans region, it is now distributed worldwide.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is a herbaceous perennial that grows into a small bush, up to 70 cm (28 in) high, with pungently-scented leaves. The leaves are light yellowish green, variously pinnatifid.
cards.imageCredit: (c) J. Sayers, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Wild Asparagus
cards.subtitle: Asparagus officinalis
cards.description: Asparagus (Asparagus officinalis) or garden asparagus is a perennial flowering plant species in the genus Asparagus native to Eurasia. Widely cultivated as a vegetable crop, its young shoots are used as a spring vegetable. In 2024, world production of asparagus was 8.9 million tonnes, led by China with 87% of the total.
cards.keyFeatures: Asparagus is an herbaceous, perennial plant growing typically to 100–150 centimetres (3–5 feet) tall, with stout stems with much-branched, feathery foliage. It has been known to grow as long as 3.5 metres (11 ft).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andreas Rockstein, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Lucerne
cards.subtitle: Medicago sativa
cards.description: Medicago sativa, commonly known as alfalfa () in North America and lucerne () in the United Kingdom, South Africa, and Australia, is a perennial flowering plant in the legume family, Fabaceae. Native to warmer temperate climates, alfalfa has long been cultivated as livestock fodder, perhaps since antiquity. It is an important forage crop in many countries around the world and is used for grazing, hay, and silage.
cards.keyFeatures: Alfalfa is a perennial forage legume which normally lives four to eight years but can live more than 20 years, depending on variety and climate. The plant grows to a height of up to 1 metre (3+1⁄2 feet).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Drepanostoma, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Drepanostoma

cards.name: Tiny Bedstraw
cards.subtitle: Galium murale
cards.description: Galium murale is a species of flowering plant in the coffee family known by the common names small goosegrass, yellow wall bedstraw and tiny bedstraw. It is native to the Mediterranean Basin of southern Europe and northern Africa, and the Middle East from Turkey and the Caucasus east to Iran and south to Saudi Arabia and Somalia. It is also considered native to the Canary Islands, Madeira and the Azores.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Daniel Cahen, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniel Cahen

cards.name: Formosa Lily
cards.subtitle: Lilium formosanum
cards.description: Lilium formosanum, also known as the Formosa lily or Taiwanese lily (traditional Chinese: 台灣百合; simplified Chinese: 台湾百合; pinyin: Táiwān bǎihé), is a plant species in the lily family, endemic to Taiwan. It is closely related to the Easter lily found in the Ryukyu Islands of Japan, eastern and northern Taiwan. Both species are cultivated for their showy, trumpet-shaped flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Lilium formosanum reaches a height of 120 to 150 cm. The bulbs are small, rounded and reach a diameter of around 2 to 4 cm.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Arnim Littek, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Arnim Littek

cards.name: Celery
cards.subtitle: Apium graveolens
cards.description: Apium graveolens, commonly known as celery, is an Old World species of flowering plant in the family Apiaceae. It was first described by Carl Linnaeus in 1753. The species is widely naturalised outside of its natural range and is used as a vegetable; modern cultivars have been selected for their leaf stalks (celery), a large bulb-like hypocotyl (celeriac), and their leaves (leaf celery).
cards.keyFeatures: Apium graveolens is a stout biennial or monocarpic perennial herb, producing flowers and seeds only once, during its second or a later year. It grows up to 1 m (3 ft) tall, with all parts of the plant having a strong celery odour.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by John Cowles

cards.name: Speckled Spur-flower
cards.subtitle: Plectranthus ciliatus
cards.description: Plectranthus ciliatus, called Indian borage, speckled spur flower, blue spur flower (a name shared with other members of its genus), and candlestick plant (shared with many other species), is a species of flowering plant in the family Lamiaceae. It is native to South Africa and Eswatini, and introduced to Victoria in Australia and the North and South Islands of New Zealand.
